signature.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
signature.detail: The reason most people come: 82 white marble domes, the world's largest hand-knotted carpet and crystal chandeliers, free to enter. Go late afternoon to see it turn gold at sunset and lit up after dark; shoulders and knees covered, abayas lent at the door.

signature.name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
signature.detail: The indoor Ferrari theme park on Yas Island, home of Formula Rossa, one of the fastest roller coasters on earth (0-240 km/h in under 5 seconds). Fully air-conditioned, so it works in summer; plan a half to full day.

signature.name: Big Ben
signature.detail: The clock tower of the Houses of Parliament and London's best-known silhouette. Best seen from Westminster Bridge or Parliament Square, and from the South Bank when it is lit up at night.

signature.name: Tower of London
signature.detail: A 1,000-year-old fortress that was palace, prison and execution site, now home of the Crown Jewels. Join a free Yeoman Warder (Beefeater) tour and go early to see the jewels before the queues build.

signature.name: Buckingham Palace
signature.detail: The King's London residence. The Changing of the Guard runs on set mornings (check the schedule); the State Rooms open to visitors for about ten weeks each summer.

signature.name: Tower Bridge
signature.detail: The Victorian bascule bridge next to the Tower of London. Walk across for free, or pay for the high walkways with glass floors 42 m above the Thames.

signature.name: Westminster Abbey
signature.detail: Coronation church since 1066 and resting place of monarchs, Newton and Darwin. Paid entry for sightseeing; attend Evensong to hear the choir for free.

signature.name: British Museum
signature.detail: Free world-history museum with the Rosetta Stone, the Parthenon sculptures and Egyptian mummies. Too big for one visit: pick three galleries and go at opening.

signature.name: London Eye
signature.detail: The 135 m observation wheel on the South Bank; a 30-minute rotation gives views over Parliament and the city. Book a timed slot and go near sunset.

signature.name: St Paul's Cathedral
signature.detail: Christopher Wren's domed masterpiece. Climb 528 steps through the Whispering Gallery to the Golden Gallery for one of the best views of the City.

signature.name: Natural History Museum
signature.detail: Free museum in a cathedral-like building in South Kensington, with dinosaurs, a blue whale skeleton and the earthquake room. Good on rainy days and with kids.

signature.name: Windsor Castle
signature.detail: The oldest occupied castle in the world, about 40 minutes by train from London. See the State Apartments and St George's Chapel; check closures for royal events before going.

signature.name: Eiffel Tower
signature.detail: The symbol of Paris. Book summit or 2nd-floor tickets online ahead; for photos go to Trocadéro, and see it sparkle for five minutes on the hour after dark.

signature.name: Louvre Museum
signature.detail: The world's most visited museum: Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Winged Victory. Timed tickets are required; enter via the Carrousel entrance and give it at least half a day.

signature.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
signature.detail: The Gothic cathedral reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire. Entry is free with a reservable time slot; the towers have a separate paid climb.

signature.name: Arc de Triomphe
signature.detail: Napoleon's triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées. Climb to the roof for the 12 avenues radiating out; use the underground passage, never cross the roundabout.

signature.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
signature.detail: White basilica on the hill of Montmartre with a free church and a panoramic view over Paris. Combine with the painters' square Place du Tertre.

signature.name: Palace of Versailles
signature.detail: Louis XIV's palace with the Hall of Mirrors and huge gardens, 40 minutes from Paris by RER C. Closed Mondays; book a timed slot and arrive at opening.

signature.name: Musée d'Orsay
signature.detail: Impressionist masterpieces (Monet, Van Gogh, Renoir) inside a former railway station. Smaller than the Louvre and doable in 2-3 hours; closed Mondays.

signature.name: Champs-Élysées
signature.detail: The grand avenue from Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe, lined with flagship stores. Walk it once, ideally at night; cafés here are pricey.

signature.name: Senso-ji
signature.detail: Tokyo's oldest temple in Asakusa, entered through the Kaminarimon gate and the Nakamise shopping street. Free and open early; go before 9 am or after dark to avoid the crowds.

signature.name: Shibuya Crossing
signature.detail: The world's busiest scramble crossing. Cross it yourself, then watch from Shibuya Sky or the Starbucks above; evenings are the most dramatic.

signature.name: Meiji Jingu
signature.detail: A Shinto shrine in a 70-hectare forest right next to Harajuku. Free; mornings are calm, and you may see a traditional wedding procession on weekends.

signature.name: Tokyo Skytree
signature.detail: At 634 m the tallest tower in Japan, with decks at 350 m and 450 m. On clear winter mornings you can see Mount Fuji; book a time slot online.

signature.name: Tokyo Tower
signature.detail: The red-and-white 1958 tower, a retro icon. Best photographed from Shiba Park or Zojo-ji temple at dusk.

signature.name: Imperial Palace
signature.detail: The Emperor's residence on the site of Edo Castle. The East Gardens are free to walk (closed Mon and Fri); the Nijubashi bridge is the classic photo.

signature.name: Statue of Liberty
signature.detail: The symbol of America on Liberty Island. Only Statue City Cruises from Battery Park lands there; book pedestal or crown tickets weeks ahead. The free Staten Island Ferry passes it without landing.

signature.name: Times Square
signature.detail: Neon heart of Midtown and the Broadway theatre district. Go after dark for the full effect; the TKTS booth sells same-day discount show tickets.

signature.name: Central Park
signature.detail: 843 acres of lawns, lakes and bridges in the middle of Manhattan. Walk from the Plaza to Bethesda Terrace and Bow Bridge, or rent a bike.

signature.name: Empire State Building
signature.detail: The 1931 Art Deco skyscraper with an open-air deck on the 86th floor. Open until late; go at sunset for day and night views in one visit.

signature.name: Brooklyn Bridge
signature.detail: The 1883 stone-and-steel bridge. Walk it from Manhattan to DUMBO (about 30 minutes) for skyline views; early morning avoids the crowds.

signature.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
signature.detail: One of the world's greatest museums, from Egyptian temples to Van Gogh. Allow half a day; the rooftop garden is open in warmer months.

signature.name: 9/11 Memorial
signature.detail: Two reflecting pools in the footprints of the Twin Towers, free and open daily. The museum below needs a timed ticket and about two hours.

signature.name: The Grand Palace
signature.detail: The former royal palace and home of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew). Strict dress code (covered shoulders and legs); go at 8:30 opening to beat heat and crowds, and ignore anyone saying it is closed.

signature.name: Wat Pho
signature.detail: Temple of the 46 m Reclining Buddha, a short walk from the Grand Palace, and the birthplace of Thai massage, which you can get on site.

signature.name: Wat Arun
signature.detail: The Temple of Dawn across the river, covered in porcelain mosaic. Take the 5-baht cross-river ferry from Tha Tien pier; best photographed from the east bank at sunset.

signature.name: Belém Tower
signature.detail: A 16th-century fortress on the Tagus that is Lisbon's most recognizable symbol, with fine Manueline carvings and river views. Go early in the morning to avoid queues, and buy tickets online in advance.

signature.name: Jerónimos Monastery
signature.detail: A vast, ornate monastery and UNESCO site that showcases Portugal's Age of Discovery. It is a short walk from Belém Tower; book a timed entry and dress respectfully.

signature.name: São Jorge Castle
signature.detail: A hilltop Moorish castle with sweeping views over the city and river. Visit in the late afternoon for cooler weather and sunset light; wear comfortable shoes for the climb.

signature.name: Praça do Comércio
signature.detail: Lisbon's grand riverside square, framed by yellow arcades and the triumphal arch. It is free to wander; come at dusk when the square is beautifully lit.

signature.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
signature.detail: A monument shaped like a ship's prow, celebrating Portugal's explorers. Combine it with Belém Tower and the monastery; the riverside promenade is ideal for a stroll.

signature.name: Santa Justa Lift
signature.detail: An ornate iron elevator linking the Baixa to Chiado, with a viewing platform at the top. Ride early or late to skip long lines, or climb the nearby streets for free views.

signature.name: Colosseum
signature.detail: The world's most famous ancient amphitheater and Rome's defining icon, where gladiators once fought before 50,000 spectators. Book timed tickets online well in advance and go at opening time to beat the crowds and heat.

signature.name: St. Peter's Basilica
signature.detail: The heart of the Vatican and one of the largest churches on earth, home to Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's baldachin. Dress code is enforced (shoulders and knees covered), and early morning visits mean shorter security lines.

signature.name: Pantheon
signature.detail: A remarkably preserved 2,000-year-old temple with the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome and its famous oculus. Entry now requires a ticket; go early or late in the day for softer light and fewer people.

signature.name: Trevi Fountain
signature.detail: Rome's most theatrical fountain, where tossing a coin over your shoulder promises a return to the city. Visit before 8am or after dark to actually see the water rather than a wall of tourists.

signature.name: Roman Forum
signature.detail: The sprawling ruins of ancient Rome's political and civic heart, best combined with the Colosseum on a single ticket. Enter from the Via dei Fori Imperiali side and wear sturdy shoes for the uneven stones.

signature.name: Vatican Museums
signature.detail: A vast art collection culminating in the Sistine Chapel's frescoes by Michelangelo. Book a timed entry online weeks ahead; Wednesday mornings are busiest, and shoulders and knees must be covered.

signature.name: Spanish Steps
signature.detail: The grand 18th-century staircase linking Piazza di Spagna to the Trinità dei Monti church, a classic Rome gathering spot. Sitting on the steps is now forbidden by law; come at sunrise for photos without crowds.

signature.name: Piazza Navona
signature.detail: A Baroque showpiece square built on an ancient stadium, with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers at its center. It is loveliest in the evening; note that cafés on the square charge premium prices.

signature.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
signature.detail: Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress, connected to the Vatican by a secret passage, with a rooftop view over the Tiber. The terrace is a superb sunset spot; buy tickets online to skip the line.

signature.name: Altare della Patria
signature.detail: The imposing white monument to Italy's unification, dominating Piazza Venezia with the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The terrace elevator gives one of Rome's best panoramic views; the monument itself is free to enter.

signature.name: Sagrada Familia
signature.detail: Gaudí's unfinished basilica is the symbol of Barcelona and unlike any church you will ever see, with soaring columns and stained-glass light. Book timed tickets online well ahead, and go early morning or late afternoon for the best light and smaller crowds.

signature.name: Park Güell
signature.detail: Gaudí's hillside garden of mosaics and playful pavilions offers sweeping views over the city. The monumental zone needs a timed ticket; arrive at opening or in the late afternoon to avoid the midday crush.

signature.name: La Rambla
signature.detail: This tree-lined promenade is the city's most famous street, linking Plaça de Catalunya to the port. Walk it in the morning, keep valuables close, and detour into the side lanes of the Gothic Quarter.

signature.name: Casa Batlló
signature.detail: Gaudí's fantastical townhouse on Passeig de Gràcia is a must for its undulating facade and dreamlike interiors. Buy skip-the-line tickets online and visit early to beat the tour groups.

signature.name: Gothic Quarter
signature.detail: The medieval core is a maze of narrow lanes, hidden squares and Roman remnants best explored on foot. Come early or in the evening for quieter streets, and wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones.

signature.name: Casa Milà
signature.detail: Known as La Pedrera, this Gaudí apartment building has a wave-like stone facade and a surreal rooftop of chimneys. Rooftop visits are timed; book online and choose a late slot for softer light.

signature.name: Mercado de La Boqueria
signature.detail: Barcelona's great market off La Rambla is a feast of jamón, seafood and fresh juice. Go before noon on a weekday for the full stalls without the worst crowds, and watch your belongings.

signature.name: Barcelona Cathedral
signature.detail: The Gothic cathedral in the heart of the old town has a cloister with geese and a quiet rooftop. Dress modestly for entry, and check opening hours since visiting times change around services.

signature.name: Camp Nou
signature.detail: The home of FC Barcelona is a pilgrimage for football fans, with a museum and stadium tour. Book tickets online in advance, and check whether the stadium is open during renovation works.

signature.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
signature.detail: The grandest of Seoul's royal palaces and the top sight for any first-time visitor, with ceremonial gates and mountain-backed courtyards. Go early morning to beat the crowds, and note the changing of the guard ceremony adds atmosphere.

signature.name: N Seoul Tower
signature.detail: The city's most recognizable landmark on Namsan, offering sweeping views over the skyline. Ride the Namsan Cable Car up and go near sunset for day-to-night views; tickets are needed for the observation deck.

signature.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
signature.detail: A hillside neighborhood of traditional hanok houses that makes for the classic Seoul photo walk. Visit on a weekday morning and keep quiet, as many buildings are private homes.

signature.name: Changdeokgung Palace and Huwon
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed palace whose Secret Garden is the highlight of many Seoul trips. The Huwon garden is visited on timed guided tours, so book ahead, especially in autumn.

signature.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
signature.detail: A striking piece of modern architecture by Zaha Hadid that anchors the city's design district. It is free to walk around outside and easy to reach by subway; evenings light it up nicely.

signature.name: Gwanghwamun Square
signature.detail: The ceremonial heart of Seoul in front of Gyeongbokgung, lined with statues and broad open space. It is a natural starting point for a palace day and is free and open at all hours.

signature.name: Myeongdong Cathedral
signature.detail: A landmark Gothic-style church set among the busy shopping streets of Myeongdong. Dress modestly and visit outside mass times for a quiet look inside.

signature.name: Jongmyo Shrine
signature.detail: A serene UNESCO royal ancestral shrine with a long, solemn hall. Visits are by guided tour only on most days, so check the schedule before you go.

signature.name: Hongdae Street
signature.detail: The youthful, energetic district around the university, known for street performances and nightlife. Come in the evening when the streets are liveliest.

signature.name: Insadong Cultural Street
signature.detail: A traditional street of tea houses, galleries and craft shops, good for souvenirs. It pairs easily with nearby palaces and is best explored on foot in the afternoon.

signature.name: Hagia Sophia
signature.detail: The defining monument of Istanbul, a vast former cathedral turned mosque whose dome and mosaics have awed visitors for nearly 1,500 years. It is the one sight no first-time visitor should skip. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds, and dress modestly since it is an active mosque.

signature.name: Topkapi Palace
signature.detail: The opulent seat of the Ottoman sultans, with courtyards, harem rooms and treasury collections overlooking the water. Allow at least half a day to explore it properly. Buy tickets in advance and arrive at opening time to avoid queues.

signature.name: Blue Mosque
signature.detail: A working mosque famous for its cascading domes and blue Iznik tiles, standing right across from Hagia Sophia. Visit outside prayer times, cover shoulders and knees, and carry a scarf for women.

signature.name: Basilica Cistern
signature.detail: An eerie underground reservoir of hundreds of columns and dim reflected light, with the famous Medusa heads. It is a cool, quick stop on hot days. Tickets are timed, so book ahead and go early or late.

signature.name: Galata Tower
signature.detail: A medieval stone tower giving the classic panorama over the Golden Horn and old city rooftops. The viewing balcony is small, so go at opening or near sunset. It sits at the end of Istiklal Avenue, easily reached on foot.

signature.name: Grand Bazaar of Istanbul
signature.detail: One of the world's oldest covered markets, a maze of thousands of shops selling carpets, jewellery and spices. It is an experience as much as a shopping stop. Go on a weekday morning, and bargain politely.

signature.name: Dolmabahce Palace
signature.detail: A lavish 19th-century waterfront palace blending European and Ottoman styles, with a spectacular ceremonial hall. Entry is by guided timed tour, so reserve a slot. It is a short walk or tram ride from the Bosphorus waterfront.

signature.name: Suleymaniye Mosque
signature.detail: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece, perched on a hill with sweeping views over the Golden Horn. It is calmer than the Blue Mosque and free to enter. Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

signature.name: Maiden's Tower
signature.detail: A tiny tower on an islet in the Bosphorus, one of the city's most photographed symbols. Boats shuttle to it from the Asian shore. Go in the late afternoon for soft light and shorter queues.

signature.name: Rumeli Fortress
signature.detail: A massive 15th-century fortress on the Bosphorus built before the Ottoman conquest, with towers and walls to climb. The walkways are steep, so wear sturdy shoes. It is best reached by boat or bus along the European shore.

signature.name: Marina Bay Sands
signature.detail: Singapore's most recognisable modern icon, with its ship-shaped SkyPark and sweeping views over the bay. Come around sunset for the best light and to catch the evening light show; book SkyPark tickets online in advance.

signature.name: Gardens by the Bay
signature.detail: A futuristic garden with the Supertree Grove and giant glass conservatories that is a must-see for first-timers. Visit in the late afternoon and stay for the free evening Supertree light show; buy conservatory tickets ahead.

signature.name: Merlion Park
signature.detail: The half-lion, half-fish Merlion is the city's emblem and the classic photo spot facing Marina Bay. Go early morning or evening to avoid the heat and crowds; it is free and an easy walk from Raffles Place MRT.

signature.name: Jewel Changi Airport
signature.detail: Home to the Rain Vortex, the world's tallest indoor waterfall, set in a lush indoor garden. It is free to enter the mall; arrive outside peak hours for clearer views and photos.

signature.name: Chinatown Heritage District
signature.detail: Historic shophouse streets packed with temples, markets and food, ideal for a first taste of old Singapore. Wander early in the day, dress respectfully at temples, and reach it easily by Chinatown MRT.

signature.name: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple
signature.detail: A striking Buddhist temple in the heart of Chinatown housing a revered relic and peaceful halls. Entry is free; wear modest clothing covering shoulders and knees, and avoid peak prayer times.

signature.name: Kampong Glam & Haji Lane
signature.detail: Colourful heritage streets around the Sultan Mosque, with boutiques and cafes along Haji Lane. Visit in the morning for cooler weather and quieter lanes; the area is a short walk from Bugis MRT.

signature.name: Little India
signature.detail: A vibrant neighbourhood of temples, markets and Indian food that feels like another world. Go on a weekday and dress modestly at Sri Mariamman Temple; reach it via Little India MRT.

signature.name: Universal Studios Singapore
signature.detail: The island's flagship theme park with rides and shows for all ages. Buy tickets online, arrive at opening, and take the Sentosa Express to reach it.

signature.name: Sydney Opera House
signature.detail: The city's defining icon, a UNESCO-listed building with a sail-shaped roof right on the harbour. It is a must-see for the architecture and the waterfront setting alone. Tip: book a guided tour in advance, and come at sunset for the best light.

signature.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
signature.detail: The huge steel arch frames the harbour and pairs perfectly with the Opera House. Walk across it for free, or climb it for the famous view. Tip: the pedestrian walkway from The Rocks is the easiest way to get onto the bridge.

signature.name: Bondi Beach
signature.detail: Australia's most famous beach, a wide curve of sand with strong surf and a lively promenade. Tip: take the train to Bondi Junction then a bus, and swim between the flags.

signature.name: The Rocks
signature.detail: The historic old town at the foot of the bridge, full of sandstone lanes, markets and pubs. Tip: come on a weekend for the markets, and walk here from Circular Quay.

signature.name: Darling Harbour
signature.detail: A busy waterfront precinct with restaurants, the aquarium and family attractions. Tip: it is an easy walk from the city centre or a short ferry ride, and evenings are liveliest.

signature.name: Royal Botanic Garden Sydney
signature.detail: A large free garden on the harbour edge with lawns, trees and views to the Opera House. Tip: enter near the Opera House and follow the path to Mrs Macquarie's Point for the classic view.

signature.name: Taronga Zoo Sydney
signature.detail: A zoo on a hillside across the harbour with native animals and skyline views. Tip: the ferry from Circular Quay is the most scenic way to arrive, and mornings are quieter.

signature.name: Burj Khalifa
signature.detail: The world's tallest building and Dubai's defining sight, with observation decks offering sweeping views over the city and desert. Book timed tickets online in advance and go near sunset for the best light, though mornings are clearer.

signature.name: Dubai Mall
signature.detail: One of the world's largest malls, packed with shops, dining and the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo inside. It sits at the foot of Burj Khalifa, so pair the two; evenings are liveliest and the metro stops right at the door.

signature.name: Palm Jumeirah
signature.detail: The famous palm-shaped artificial island lined with beaches, hotels and marinas. Drive or take a taxi across it, and stop at the viewing points for photos of the fronds and the skyline.

signature.name: Dubai Fountain
signature.detail: A choreographed fountain show set in the lake beside Dubai Mall and Burj Khalifa. Shows run in the evening; arrive early to grab a spot along the promenade for the best view.

signature.name: Burj Al Arab
signature.detail: The sail-shaped luxury hotel that became a symbol of modern Dubai. It is best seen and photographed from the nearby beaches; access to the interior is limited to guests and diners.

signature.name: Museum of the Future
signature.detail: A striking torus-shaped building housing exhibits on future technology and design. Book tickets ahead as slots fill up, and allow a couple of hours to explore the floors.

signature.name: The Dubai Frame
signature.detail: A giant picture-frame structure with a glass skywalk linking two towers and views over old and new Dubai. Visit in the late afternoon for cooler temperatures and good light.

signature.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
signature.detail: A preserved old-town quarter of wind-tower houses, courtyards and narrow lanes along Dubai Creek. Go in the morning to wander quietly, then take an abra across the creek.

signature.name: Charles Bridge
signature.detail: Prague's most iconic sight, a 14th-century stone bridge lined with baroque statues and framed by the castle skyline. Go at sunrise to enjoy it before the crowds arrive, and note it is pedestrian-only.

signature.name: Prague Castle
signature.detail: The vast hilltop complex is the historic seat of Czech rulers and dominates the city's skyline. Book castle circuit tickets online and allow at least half a day; it is a steep uphill walk or a short tram ride from Lesser Town.

signature.name: Old Town Square
signature.detail: The heart of the old city, ringed by colorful facades and home to the famous astronomical clock. Come a few minutes before the hour to see the clock's apostles perform, but expect big crowds.

signature.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
signature.detail: A soaring Gothic cathedral inside Prague Castle with stunning stained glass and royal tombs. Dress respectfully and arrive early, as security lines at the castle grow quickly after mid-morning.

signature.name: Prague Astronomical Clock
signature.detail: A medieval mechanical marvel on the Old Town Hall that draws a crowd every hour for its moving figures. Stand to the side for a better view, and consider climbing the tower for rooftop views over the square.

signature.name: Petřín Lookout Tower
signature.detail: A miniature Eiffel-style tower on a green hill offering the best panorama of the city. Walk up through the park or take the funicular, then climb the stairs for the view on a clear day.

signature.name: Church of Our Lady before Týn
signature.detail: The twin Gothic spires rising over Old Town Square are one of Prague's defining images. The interior is free to enter and quieter than the square outside; check opening hours before visiting.

signature.name: Dancing House
signature.detail: A playful modern landmark by the river designed by Gehry and Milunić. View it from the riverside embankment, and book ahead if you want to visit the rooftop bar for views.

signature.name: Zocalo
signature.detail: The vast main square is the heart of Mexico City and the natural starting point for any first visit, ringed by the National Palace and the cathedral. Come early in the morning for cooler air and fewer crowds, and note that the flag ceremony happens here daily.

signature.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City
signature.detail: This enormous colonial cathedral anchors the Zocalo and is one of the most important churches in the Americas. It is free to enter but modest dress is expected, and it sits right beside the metro and the square.

signature.name: National Palace
signature.detail: The seat of the federal government faces the Zocalo and is famous for the murals inside. Bring photo ID for entry, check opening hours in advance, and go on a weekday morning to avoid queues.

signature.name: Chapultepec Castle
signature.detail: Perched on the hill in Chapultepec Park, this castle offers city views and grand rooms that make it a top stop. Arrive when it opens to beat the line, and be ready for a steep walk up or a short park train ride.

signature.name: National Museum of Anthropology
signature.detail: One of the world's great museums, with the Aztec Sun Stone and vast halls on Mexico's ancient cultures. Allow at least half a day, and note that it is usually closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
signature.detail: The Blue House in Coyoacan draws visitors from around the world to see where Kahlo lived and worked. Book timed tickets online well ahead, as walk-up entry is often sold out.

signature.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
signature.detail: The most visited Catholic shrine in the Americas, home to the image of the Virgin of Guadalupe. Go on a weekday morning for a calmer visit, and dress respectfully; it is reachable by metro plus a short walk.

signature.name: Templo Mayor
signature.detail: The excavated Aztec main temple sits right beside the Zocalo, giving a striking sense of the city's layered past. Combine it with the cathedral next door and go early to avoid midday heat.

signature.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
signature.detail: This marble palace is the city's cultural showpiece, with murals and a grand theater hall. Check the schedule for performances, or simply admire the exterior and the neighboring Alameda park.

signature.name: Angel of Independence
signature.detail: The golden angel on Paseo de la Reforma is the city's most recognizable monument and a lively gathering point. Visit at dusk when it is lit, and use the nearby metro or a short walk along the avenue.

signature.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
signature.detail: This is the memorial and mausoleum of Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah, and the most visited sight in Accra. It combines a museum, gardens and the tomb itself, so it gives a first-time visitor the country's modern history in one stop. Go in the morning to avoid the midday heat, and bring small cash for the modest entry fee.

signature.name: Independence Square, Accra
signature.detail: This vast ceremonial square on the coast is where Ghana marks its independence, with the Black Star Gate and memorial arches as its icons. It is free to walk around and best visited early morning or late afternoon for cooler air and better light. It sits close to Osu, so you can combine it with a walk through that district.

signature.name: Osu Castle
signature.detail: A centuries-old coastal fort that served as seat of government for much of Ghana's history, it is a key stop for understanding the city's colonial and post-independence past. Access is often restricted because it remains a state building, so check opening arrangements before you go rather than assuming you can walk in. It is a short drive from Independence Square.

signature.name: Makola Market
signature.detail: Accra's biggest and busiest market is a full sensory experience of food, fabric and everyday commerce, and it is a must for seeing the city at work. Go early in the morning when it is cooler and less crowded, and keep valuables close in the narrow lanes. It is central and easy to reach by taxi or trotro.

signature.name: Jamestown Lighthouse
signature.detail: The lighthouse stands over the old Jamestown harbour, one of the city's oldest quarters, with good views over the fishing community and coastline. Come in the late afternoon for softer light and a walk around the nearby streets. It is west of the centre and best reached by taxi.

signature.name: Amman Citadel
signature.detail: The hilltop site where Amman's history layers from Roman to Umayyad times, with the Temple of Hercules columns and the Umayyad palace remains. It is the city's defining sight and gives wide views over downtown. Go early morning or late afternoon for cooler weather and better light; it is a short taxi ride from downtown.

signature.name: Roman Theater
signature.detail: A well-preserved 2nd-century Roman theater cut into the hillside, still used for performances. Its scale and setting make it a must-see for first-time visitors. Visit in the morning to avoid the midday heat; it is a short walk from downtown and the Citadel.

signature.name: Anne Frank House
signature.detail: The secret annex where Anne Frank wrote her diary is a deeply moving must-see. Book tickets online well in advance; they sell out and are timed-entry only.

signature.name: Van Gogh Museum
signature.detail: Houses the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings, including Almond Blossom and Wheatfield with Crows. Reserve a timed ticket online and go early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Rijksmuseum
signature.detail: The Dutch national museum, home to The Night Watch and The Milkmaid. Book online, and don't miss the stunning Rijksmuseum Library inside.

signature.name: Canal Ring
signature.detail: The UNESCO-listed ring of canals is the city's iconic backdrop, best explored on foot or by boat. Early morning or evening gives the best light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Dam Square
signature.detail: The historic heart of Amsterdam, flanked by the Royal Palace and close to the Red Light District. It's a central meeting point and easy to reach on foot from Centraal Station.

signature.name: Red Light District
signature.detail: A unique urban hub and one of the city's oldest quarters, known for its narrow alleys and window brothels. Visit respectfully, keep photos to yourself, and go with a guide if you want context.

signature.name: Parthenon
signature.detail: The iconic temple on the Acropolis is the symbol of ancient Greece and a must-see for any first-time visitor. Go early in the morning to avoid crowds and heat; buy a combined ticket that includes other sites.

signature.name: Acropolis Museum
signature.detail: This modern museum houses the treasures of the Acropolis, including the Parthenon sculptures, with stunning views of the hill. Visit in the late afternoon for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds; tickets can be bought online.

signature.name: Plaka
signature.detail: The charming old town at the foot of the Acropolis is perfect for strolling through narrow streets lined with shops and tavernas. Wear comfortable shoes and explore early evening when the area comes alive.

signature.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
signature.detail: This ancient marketplace was the heart of classical Athens and offers a peaceful escape from the city bustle. The Temple of Hephaestus here is one of the best-preserved Greek temples; go early to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
signature.detail: These massive columns are a testament to ancient ambition and are especially magical at sunset. Combine your visit with Hadrian's Arch next door; the site is compact and quick to see.

signature.name: Syntagma Square
signature.detail: The central square is home to the Greek Parliament and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, guarded by evzones. Catch the changing of the guard every hour; it's free and a great photo opportunity.

signature.name: Panathenaic Stadium
signature.detail: The all-marble stadium hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896 and offers a unique glimpse into sports history. Climb to the top for panoramic views; audio guides are available and worth it.

signature.name: Sky Tower
signature.detail: Auckland's defining landmark, rising above the central city and offering the best views of the harbour, islands and volcanic cones. It is a must-see for first-time visitors. Tip: go up in the late afternoon for daylight views and stay for sunset; book tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: Auckland War Memorial Museum
signature.detail: Set in Auckland Domain, this museum holds major Maori and Pacific collections and tells the story of New Zealand's people and wars. It is a must-see for cultural context. Tip: allow at least two hours and check opening hours before you go, as they vary by season.

signature.name: Viaduct Harbour
signature.detail: The lively waterfront district where you can walk among boats and enjoy the harbour atmosphere. It is a must-see for a relaxed stroll near the city centre. Tip: visit in the evening when the waterfront is at its liveliest.

signature.name: Auckland Harbour Bridge
signature.detail: The bridge is an icon of the city's harbour and a great photo subject, especially from the water or nearby viewpoints. It is a must-see for understanding Auckland's geography. Tip: see it from a harbour ferry or a waterfront walk rather than driving across.

signature.name: Waiheke Island
signature.detail: A short ferry ride from the city, this island is known for its beaches and relaxed pace, making it a favourite day trip. It is a must-see if you have a full day. Tip: take an early ferry to make the most of the day and check return times in advance.

signature.name: Piha Beach
signature.detail: A dramatic west-coast beach with black sand and rugged scenery, a classic Auckland day out. It is a must-see for nature lovers. Tip: it is best reached by car, and the surf can be strong, so swim between the flags.

signature.name: Glenelg Beach
signature.detail: Adelaide's classic seaside escape, with a long sandy beach, a lively pier and a tram that runs straight from the city centre. It is the easiest place to combine a city break with a swim. Take the tram from Victoria Square; go on a warm afternoon and stay for sunset over the water.

signature.name: Adelaide Central Market
signature.detail: A buzzing indoor market in the heart of the city, packed with fresh produce, cheese, coffee and small eateries. It is the best single place to taste local South Australian food. Visit on a weekday morning when it is busy but not crammed, and bring cash for small stalls.

signature.name: Adelaide Botanic Garden
signature.detail: A large, free garden next to the city centre with glasshouses, a rose garden and shady paths. It is a peaceful must-see for anyone wanting a break from the streets. Enter from North Terrace and go early in the day to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Art Gallery of South Australia
signature.detail: One of Australia's finest art museums, with strong Australian and Indigenous collections and a grand historic facade on North Terrace. Entry is free, making it an easy must-see. Check opening hours before you go, as it closes in the evening.

signature.name: Hahndorf
signature.detail: A historic German-settled village in the Adelaide Hills, known for its main street of old buildings, bakeries and craft shops. It is a popular day trip from the city. It is easiest to reach by car or a organised tour; go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

signature.name: National Wine Centre of Australia
signature.detail: A modern wine museum and tasting venue at the edge of the Botanic Garden, introducing the wines of South Australia's regions. It is a good first stop for anyone planning to explore wine country. Book a tasting in advance and walk there from North Terrace.

signature.name: Coopers Brewery
signature.detail: Australia's largest independent family-owned brewery, a landmark for beer lovers. Tours show the brewing process and end with tastings. Tours must be booked ahead and run on set days, so check times before travelling to the site.

signature.name: Adelaide Showgrounds
signature.detail: A large events and amusement site best known for hosting the annual Royal Adelaide Show. It is worth checking what is on during your visit. It is a short tram or train ride from the city centre; buy tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: Sabarmati Ashram
signature.detail: This riverside ashram was Mahatma Gandhi's home and base during India's freedom struggle, making it the city's most meaningful pilgrimage for visitors. Go early morning to avoid heat and crowds; entry is free, and the museum is closed on some public holidays, so check ahead.

signature.name: Adalaj Stepwell
signature.detail: A stunning five-storey stepwell carved with intricate Hindu and Islamic motifs, it is one of Gujarat's finest architectural treasures and a photographer's dream. It lies about 18 km north of the city; hire a taxi or auto for the half-day trip, and visit in the cooler morning hours.

signature.name: Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad
signature.detail: Built in 1424, this mosque in the old city is famed for its yellow sandstone arches and the shaking minarets nearby, and it anchors the bustling heritage quarter. Dress modestly, remove shoes, and avoid prayer times; it is a short walk from Bhadra Fort.

signature.name: Bhadra Fort
signature.detail: The 15th-century fort founded by Ahmed Shah marks the origin of Ahmedabad and now hosts a lively evening market and cultural events. Come after 5 pm when the stalls open and the heat fades; the fort itself is free to enter.

signature.name: Sarkhej Roza
signature.detail: A serene complex of tombs and mosques often called the 'Acropolis of Ahmedabad', it blends Islamic and Hindu architectural styles in a peaceful lakeside setting. It is about 8 km southwest of the centre; go at sunset for the best light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Kankaria Lake
signature.detail: A circular 15th-century lake turned family recreation hub, with a zoo, toy train and evening fountain shows, it is the city's favourite outdoor escape. Visit in the late afternoon; the lakefront promenade is free, though individual attractions charge small fees.

signature.name: Kok Tobe Tower
signature.detail: The city's most famous landmark, a TV tower on a hill above Almaty with sweeping views over the mountains and the city. Ride the cable car up from the city center, or take a taxi; go in the late afternoon for the best light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Ascension Cathedral
signature.detail: A striking wooden cathedral in Panfilov Park, famous for being built without nails and surviving earthquakes. It is an active church, so dress modestly and keep quiet inside; visit in the morning when it is quieter.

signature.name: Medeu
signature.detail: A high-altitude mountain sports complex in a dramatic gorge, a classic Almaty excursion. Check opening times before you go and bring a warm layer, as it sits well above the city and is much cooler.

signature.name: Shymbulak
signature.detail: A mountain resort reached by cable car from Medeu, popular for skiing in winter and hiking in summer. Go on a clear day for the best views and buy your cable car ticket at the base station.

signature.name: Big Almaty Lake
signature.detail: A turquoise alpine lake set in the mountains above the city, one of the region's most photographed sights. Access can be restricted at times, so check locally before setting out, and go early to avoid afternoon traffic.

signature.name: Panfilov Park
signature.detail: A leafy central park that holds the Ascension Cathedral and the Golden Warrior Monument, an easy and pleasant stop. It is free to enter and best visited on a mild morning combined with the nearby cathedral.

signature.name: Central State Museum of Kazakhstan
signature.detail: The country's main museum, with collections on Kazakh history, archaeology and culture. Allow a couple of hours, and check the day's opening hours since museums here often close one day a week.

signature.name: Zelionyj Bazar
signature.detail: A lively green market where you can see local produce, dried fruit, spices and dairy. Go in the morning when it is busiest and freshest, and bring small cash for purchases.

signature.name: Antwerp Central Station
signature.detail: Widely ranked among the world's most beautiful railway stations, with a soaring stone concourse and layered platforms that make arriving in Antwerp an event in itself. It is still a working station, so visit outside the morning and evening rush for the best photos, and note that it sits at the end of the main shopping street, a short walk from the old town.

signature.name: Cathedral of Our Lady, Antwerp
signature.detail: The city's tallest church and its defining spire, home to major Rubens paintings and centuries of history. Go early in the day to avoid queues, and check opening hours before you travel as they vary by season.

signature.name: Grote Markt
signature.detail: The historic square at the heart of the old town, ringed by ornate guild houses and the city hall, and the natural starting point for a first walk. It is free and open at all hours; come in the morning for quieter photos or in the evening for the lit-up facades.

signature.name: Het Steen
signature.detail: Antwerp's medieval castle on the Scheldt, the oldest surviving building in the city and a compact, atmospheric stop. It is close to the Grote Markt, so pair the two on foot, and check current opening times as the site has been redeveloped for visitors.

signature.name: Museum aan de Stroom
signature.detail: A striking modern museum whose rooftop panorama over the port and city is a highlight in its own right. The rooftop is reachable separately from the exhibitions; go late afternoon for the best light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Rubens House
signature.detail: The preserved home and studio of the painter Peter Paul Rubens, one of the city's essential art stops. Book ahead in peak season, as entry is timed and capacity is limited.

signature.name: Plantin-Moretus Museum
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed printing house and family home that tells the story of early modern publishing in Antwerp. It is a quieter alternative to the big art museums and rewards a slow visit; check opening days, as many Antwerp museums close on Mondays.

signature.name: Georgia Aquarium
signature.detail: One of the largest aquariums in the world and Atlanta's top draw, with whale sharks and beluga whales among its headline exhibits. Book timed-entry tickets online in advance, especially for weekends and school holidays, and arrive early to beat the crowds.

signature.name: World of Coca-Cola
signature.detail: A museum devoted to the famous soft drink, next to Centennial Olympic Park, with tasting rooms and company history. Allow a couple of hours and buy tickets online to skip the queue.

signature.name: Centennial Olympic Park
signature.detail: A downtown park built for the 1996 Olympics, with the Fountain of Rings as its centerpiece. It is free and open daily; visit in the late afternoon for cooler weather and the fountain shows.

signature.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
signature.detail: Preserves the birthplace, church and legacy of Martin Luther King Jr., making it essential for understanding the city's civil rights history. Entry to the park sites is free; check hours for the birth home and visitor center before you go.

signature.name: High Museum of Art
signature.detail: Atlanta's leading art museum, known for its collection and striking buildings in Midtown. It is closed on some weekdays, so check the schedule and consider a combined ticket if offered.

signature.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
signature.detail: A large garden next to Piedmont Park with seasonal displays and a canopy walk. Go in the morning for cooler temperatures and easier parking.

signature.name: Fox Theatre
signature.detail: A historic 1920s theater with an ornate Moorish-inspired interior, hosting shows and tours. Check the calendar for performances or guided tours, and book ahead for popular acts.

signature.name: Texas State Capitol
signature.detail: The seat of Texas government and the city's most recognizable historic building, with a dome taller than the US Capitol's. Free self-guided tours run daily; go early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat and crowds, and note that the building is a short walk north of downtown.

signature.name: Lady Bird Lake
signature.detail: A calm river-like lake in the heart of the city, lined with a popular hike-and-bike trail and skyline views. Rent a kayak or walk the trail at sunrise or sunset for the best light and cooler temperatures.

signature.name: Barton Springs Pool
signature.detail: A spring-fed natural pool that stays cool year-round and is a beloved Austin ritual. Bring cash or check the city site for entry fees, arrive early on summer weekends, and expect a short walk from nearby parking.

signature.name: Zilker Park
signature.detail: Austin's central green space, next to Barton Springs and Lady Bird Lake, great for picnics and skyline views. Visit on a weekday or early morning; it is easy to reach by bike or rideshare and gets busy during events.

signature.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
signature.detail: A well-run museum telling the story of Texas from early settlement to the modern era. Allow two to three hours, check ticket prices online, and go on a weekday for a quieter visit; it sits near the Capitol.

signature.name: University of Texas at Austin
signature.detail: A large, lively campus that anchors the city's culture and is worth a stroll for its architecture and museums. Walk the main mall in the morning, and check whether visitor parking or guided campus tours are available in advance.

signature.name: COTALAND
signature.detail: A motorsport-themed amusement park outside central Austin, best for families and thrill-seekers. Buy tickets online, check opening days before you go, and plan for a car or rideshare since it is not walkable from downtown.

signature.name: Icherisheher
signature.detail: The walled Old Town is Baku's heart and a UNESCO-listed maze of lanes, caravanserais and courtyards. It is the best place to start a first visit. Go early morning to avoid crowds and heat; it is walkable from the city centre and free to enter.

signature.name: Maiden Tower of Baku
signature.detail: This mysterious cylindrical tower inside Icherisheher is the city's symbol and offers views over the Old Town and bay. Climb it for the panorama and the small museum. Buy a ticket on site and go on a weekday morning to skip queues.

signature.name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
signature.detail: A 15th-century royal complex with a courtyard, mausoleum and palace rooms, right inside the Old Town. It pairs naturally with the Maiden Tower on a walking day. Check opening hours before you go and allow about an hour.

signature.name: Flame Towers
signature.detail: The three flame-shaped skyscrapers are Baku's modern icon and glow at night. Best seen from Baku Boulevard after dark. You cannot usually go up, so plan a walk along the seafront for the view.

signature.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
signature.detail: Zaha Hadid's flowing white building is a must for architecture fans and houses exhibitions inside. The exterior is photogenic from every angle. Take a taxi or metro and check exhibition tickets in advance.

signature.name: Baku Boulevard
signature.detail: A long Caspian seafront promenade for strolling, with the Flame Towers and carpet museum nearby. It is ideal at sunset. It is free and easy to reach from the centre on foot.

signature.name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
signature.detail: The building shaped like a rolled carpet sits on the boulevard and holds a rich collection of Azerbaijani carpets. It is a good indoor stop on hot or rainy days. Combine it with a boulevard walk.

signature.name: Ateshgah of Baku
signature.detail: The fire temple at Surakhany is a historic site of fire worship on the Absheron Peninsula. It is a short trip outside the centre. Go with a taxi or tour and allow half a day with Yanar Dag.

signature.name: Yanar Dag
signature.detail: A hillside where natural gas keeps a fire burning, a striking sight tied to Azerbaijan's 'land of fire' identity. It is outside the city, so pair it with Ateshgah. Visit in the evening for the best effect.

signature.name: National Aquarium
signature.detail: Baltimore's most famous attraction, with sharks, dolphins and a rainforest under one roof on the Inner Harbor. Book timed tickets online in advance, especially on weekends and school holidays, and arrive early to beat the crowds.

signature.name: Inner Harbor
signature.detail: The city's waterfront heart, packed with shops, restaurants and views of the harbor. It is free to stroll; go in the morning or at sunset for the best light and fewer crowds, and it is an easy walk from downtown hotels.

signature.name: Fort McHenry
signature.detail: The star-shaped fort that inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner' during the War of 1812. Allow a couple of hours for the visitor center and ramparts; it is a short drive or water taxi ride from the Inner Harbor.

signature.name: American Visionary Art Museum
signature.detail: A one-of-a-kind museum devoted to self-taught artists, with wildly creative exhibits and a giant whirligig outside. Check opening days before you go, as it closes early in the week, and leave time for the gift shop.

signature.name: George Peabody Library
signature.detail: A breathtaking 19th-century library with cast-iron balconies and a soaring atrium, often called one of the most beautiful in the world. It is free to visit during open hours; go on a weekday morning for quiet photos.

signature.name: Maryland Science Center
signature.detail: A hands-on science museum with an IMAX theater and a planetarium, great for families. Buy tickets online to skip lines and check showtimes for the planetarium before you arrive.

signature.name: Johns Hopkins University
signature.detail: One of America's leading universities, with a handsome Homewood campus worth a walk. It is a short ride north of downtown; stroll the quads on a weekday when the campus is lively.

signature.name: Oriole Park at Camden Yards
signature.detail: A beloved ballpark that helped spark the retro-stadium trend, right by downtown. Catch a game if the Orioles are in town, and buy tickets early for popular summer matchups.

food: Casual meal $12-20; crab cakes and seafood dinners $25-45
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $130-220 a night

signature.name: Forbidden City
signature.detail: The world's largest palace complex and the heart of imperial China for five centuries, with 9,000 rooms of halls, courtyards and treasures. Book tickets online in advance (passport required) and go early on a weekday to avoid the biggest crowds.

signature.name: Great Wall of China
signature.detail: The iconic ancient fortification winding over mountains north of Beijing, a bucket-list sight and UNESCO site. The Mutianyu section is the most visitor-friendly; take the cable car up and walk the restored ramparts, ideally in the morning.

signature.name: Summer Palace
signature.detail: A vast imperial garden of lakes, pavilions and long corridors that was the Qing court's summer retreat. Allow half a day, arrive at opening, and wear comfortable shoes for the lakeside walks.

signature.name: Temple of Heaven
signature.detail: A masterpiece of Ming architecture where emperors prayed for good harvests, set in a large park used by locals for tai chi. Visit early morning to see the park life, then enter the main halls with a combo ticket.

signature.name: Tiananmen Square
signature.detail: One of the world's largest public squares, flanked by the Gate of Heavenly Peace and major museums. Security checks are strict, so carry your passport and avoid bringing large bags.

signature.name: Bird's Nest
signature.detail: The striking National Stadium from the 2008 Olympics, a modern icon best seen lit up at night. Combine it with a stroll in the Olympic Park; the exterior is free to view.

signature.name: Ming Tombs
signature.detail: The burial complex of thirteen Ming emperors in a mountain valley, with the grand Sacred Way and the excavated Dingling tomb. It is far from the city, so pair it with the Great Wall on a day trip.

signature.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
signature.detail: Beirut's most recognizable landmark, with its blue domes and tall minarets dominating Martyrs' Square. It is a must-see for its scale and central location. Dress modestly and remove shoes before entering; visit outside prayer times.

signature.name: Pigeon Rocks
signature.detail: Dramatic natural rock arches rising from the sea, best viewed from the Corniche. A classic Beirut photo spot and a pleasant walk. Go at sunset for the best light; the area is free and open.

signature.name: National Museum of Beirut
signature.detail: Houses an excellent collection of archaeological treasures spanning millennia. Essential for understanding Lebanon's history. Check opening hours (usually closed Mondays); tickets are affordable.

signature.name: Jeita Grotto
signature.detail: A stunning cave system with vast chambers and underground river, a short drive from Beirut. A top natural attraction. Boats operate in the lower grotto; photography is restricted inside.

signature.name: Byblos Citadel
signature.detail: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a crusader castle and Roman ruins. A rewarding day trip from Beirut. Wear comfortable shoes for the uneven site; allow half a day.

signature.name: Beit Beirut
signature.detail: A moving museum of modern history housed in a bullet-scarred building on the Green Line. Offers insight into the civil war. Check opening days; entry is often free or by donation.

signature.name: Sursock Museum
signature.detail: A beautiful villa showcasing Lebanese and regional modern art. The building itself is a gem. Closed Mondays; combine with a walk in the nearby Sursock district.

signature.name: Our Lady of Lebanon
signature.detail: A major Christian pilgrimage site with a towering statue overlooking the bay of Jounieh. Worth the trip for the views and spiritual atmosphere. Take the cable car up for a scenic ride.

signature.name: Beiteddine Palace
signature.detail: A magnificent 19th-century palace in the Chouf mountains, known for its architecture and gardens. A cultural highlight. Combine with a visit to Deir el Qamar; check for festival schedules.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $2 a night for two

signature.name: Belgrade Fortress
signature.detail: The ancient core of the city, where Roman, Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian layers sit above the meeting of the Sava and Danube rivers. It is free to wander and the riverside views at sunset are the highlight. Go in late afternoon and wear comfortable shoes for the uneven cobbles.

signature.name: Knez Mihailova Street
signature.detail: Belgrade's main pedestrian spine, lined with 19th-century facades, cafes and shops, connecting the fortress area to Republic Square. It is the natural place to start a walking day and to people-watch in the evening. Visit early morning for quiet photos or after dark when it is liveliest.

signature.name: St. Sava Temple
signature.detail: One of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, its huge dome dominates the Vračar skyline and the gold mosaic interior is striking. Entry is free and modest dress is expected. It is a short walk or trolleybus ride from the city center; go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Skadarlija
signature.detail: A cobbled bohemian quarter of old kafanas and live music, the classic spot for a traditional Serbian evening. It is best experienced at dinner time when the street comes alive. Reserve a table in advance on weekends.

signature.name: Nikola Tesla Museum
signature.detail: A small but fascinating museum holding Tesla's personal archive and working demonstrations of his inventions. Guided tours run on a schedule and are the only way to see the exhibits. Check tour times and arrive early, as groups fill up.

signature.name: Sava River
signature.detail: The riverfront and its floating splavovi clubs and cafes are central to Belgrade's social life, with good views from the fortress and the bridges. A riverside walk is an easy, free way to see the city from another angle. Evenings are the most atmospheric time.

signature.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
signature.detail: Bengaluru's most beloved green space, home to a famous glasshouse and centuries-old trees. Go early morning for cool air and fewer crowds; the garden is closed on some public holidays, so check ahead.

signature.name: Bangalore Palace
signature.detail: A Tudor-style royal residence with carved wood interiors and a trove of royal memorabilia. It sits in the north of the city; a taxi or auto is the easiest way to reach it, and an entry ticket is required.

signature.name: Cubbon Park
signature.detail: A vast central park of shaded avenues right in the heart of the city, ideal for a morning walk. It is free to enter and easily reached by metro; weekends are liveliest.

signature.name: ISKCON Temple Bangalore
signature.detail: A large hilltop temple complex that is one of the city's most visited religious sites. Dress modestly, expect security checks, and visit in the evening when the temple is lit up.

signature.name: Vidhana Soudha
signature.detail: The imposing seat of the state legislature, a landmark of neo-Dravidian architecture. It is best viewed from outside; the illuminated facade after dark is the highlight, and photography inside is not allowed.

signature.name: Wonderla (Bangalore)
signature.detail: A big amusement and water park on the city's outskirts, popular with families. Plan a full day, book tickets online in advance, and arrange transport since it is well outside the centre.

signature.name: Brandenburg Gate
signature.detail: Berlin's defining monument and the symbol of the city's reunification, standing where the Wall once divided East and West. signature.name: Reichstag Building
signature.detail: The German parliament's glass-domed home offers free rooftop views over the city and a close look at its modern architecture. signature.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
signature.detail: This open-air site on Bernauer Strasse preserves a stretch of the Wall, the death strip and a viewing tower, making the division of the city tangible. It is free and best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive. Take the U8 or S-Bahn to Bernauer Strasse.

signature.name: Checkpoint Charlie
signature.detail: The famous Cold War crossing point is a quick but essential stop for understanding Berlin's divided past. The outdoor site is free and always accessible, though the nearby museum charges admission. Visit early or late in the day, as the corner gets very crowded midday.

signature.name: Pergamon Museum
signature.detail: Home to monumental reconstructions such as the Pergamon Altar and the Ishtar Gate, this is one of the world's great archaeology museums. Tickets are timed and sell out, so book online in advance. Note that parts of the museum may be closed for long-term renovation, so check before you go.

signature.name: Berlin Cathedral
signature.detail: This grand Protestant church on Museum Island impresses with its dome and ornate interior, and the climb to the dome gallery rewards you with rooftop views. There is an admission fee for the interior and dome. Dress modestly and go on a weekday morning to avoid queues.

signature.name: East Side Gallery
signature.detail: The longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall, now an open-air gallery of murals along the Spree River. It is free and open at all hours; walk it in the morning light. Reach it via Ostbahnhof or Warschauer Strasse stations.

signature.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
signature.detail: Daniel Libeskind's striking building and its exhibits trace German-Jewish history and the Holocaust with unusual emotional power. Tickets are timed and best booked online. Allow at least two hours and take the U-Bahn to Hallesches Tor.

signature.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
signature.detail: The field of concrete steles near the Brandenburg Gate is a solemn, powerful memorial, with an underground information centre beneath it. Entry is free, and the centre is closed on Mondays. Visit at dusk for a quieter, more reflective experience.

signature.name: Sanssouci Palace
signature.detail: Frederick the Great's rococo summer palace in Potsdam, surrounded by terraced vineyards and parkland, is a rewarding half-day trip from Berlin. Palace entry is timed and limited, so reserve tickets online. Take the regional train to Potsdam and allow time to wander the gardens.

signature.detail: The city's flagship museum, home to a celebrated Pre-Raphaelite art collection and wide-ranging displays on Birmingham's history. Entry is free, so it is an easy must-see; check opening days before you go as galleries sometimes close for rotation.

signature.name: St Philip's Cathedral
signature.detail: A compact but striking cathedral in the heart of the city, known for its Burne-Jones stained-glass windows. It is free to enter and makes a peaceful pause between the shops; visit on a weekday morning for the quietest experience.

signature.detail: This hilltop sanctuary sits at the end of the world's longest portico, a rewarding walk with views over the city. Take the walk or the San Luca Express from the centre, and allow a half day for the round trip.

signature.name: Museum of Fine Arts
signature.detail: One of the largest art museums in the United States, with a collection spanning ancient to contemporary art, including works by Rembrandt, Monet, and Van Gogh. signature.detail: A sheltered cove where you can watch African penguins up close from boardwalks and sometimes share the sand with them. Go early or late to avoid the midday crowds, and bring a windbreaker since the Cape wind can be strong.

signature.detail: This vast garden at the foot of Table Mountain showcases South Africa's unique flora, with a famous treetop walkway and seasonal blooms. Allow at least half a day, wear comfortable shoes, and consider a picnic on the lawns.

signature.name: Bo-Kaap

signature.detail: Home to the Book of Kells and the stunning Long Room, this library is a must-see for its history and architecture. Tickets are timed and sell out quickly, so reserve online ahead; visit right at opening for a quieter experience.

signature.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
signature.detail: Ireland's largest cathedral, founded in 1220, offers stunning Gothic architecture and a rich history. Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and consider attending a choral evensong for a memorable experience.

signature.name: Kilmainham Gaol
signature.detail: This former prison is a powerful symbol of Ireland's struggle for independence, with guided tours telling poignant stories. Tours often sell out, so book tickets online well in advance; it's a short tram ride from the city center.

signature.name: Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin
signature.detail: Dublin's oldest cathedral, dating back to the 11th century, features a beautiful crypt and stunning medieval architecture. Combine your visit with Dublin Castle nearby, and check for evensong times to hear the choir.

signature.detail: One of Germany's tallest skyscrapers, offering an open-air observation deck with panoramic views over Frankfurt and the Rhine-Main region. It is a must for skyline lovers. signature.name: Römer
signature.detail: Frankfurt's historic town hall, a medieval building that has served as the city's administrative center for centuries. Its distinctive facade is a symbol of the city. Tip: the inner courtyard is free to visit and less crowded than the square outside.

signature.name: Eiserner Steg
signature.detail: A pedestrian bridge over the Main River, famous for its love locks and views of the skyline. It is a romantic and practical crossing between the old town and Sachsenhausen. Tip: walk across at dusk for beautiful reflections of the city lights on the water.

signature.name: Goethe House
signature.detail: The birthplace of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, now a museum dedicated to his life and work. It offers a glimpse into 18th-century Frankfurt. Tip: check the website for opening hours and consider a combined ticket with the nearby Goethe Museum.

signature.name: St. Paul's Church
signature.detail: A historic church that served as the seat of the first German National Assembly in 1848, making it a symbol of German democracy. It is a must-see for history buffs. Tip: entry is free, but donations are welcome; climb the tower for a view over the city center.

signature.name: Palmengarten

signature.name: Zoo Frankfurt

signature.name: West Lake Park
signature.detail: A classic city lake with pavilions, walkways and gardens, good for a relaxed stroll or a boat ride. Late afternoon is the pleasantest time, and entry to the park itself is generally free.

signature.name: United Nations Office at Geneva
signature.detail: One of the world's key diplomatic sites, set in the Ariana park with the famous broken chair outside. Guided visits require booking ahead and a passport for security; check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire

signature.name: Téléphérique du Salève

signature.detail: The city's classic green escape, with cable car access, walking trails and panoramic views over Guangzhou. Visit early morning when locals exercise and haze is lighter; take the cable car up and walk down if time allows.

signature.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
signature.detail: A grand memorial building honoring the revolutionary leader, set in gardens and central to modern Chinese history. Combine it with nearby Yuexiu Park; check opening hours as the interior can close earlier than the grounds.

signature.name: Space Center Houston
signature.detail: The official visitor center of NASA's Johnson Space Center, this is the one place in Houston that draws travelers from around the world, with real spacecraft and astronaut history on display. Book tickets online in advance and go early on weekday mornings to beat the crowds; it sits well south of downtown, so plan on a car or rideshare.

signature.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
signature.detail: One of the largest art museums in the country, with a broad collection spanning antiquity to contemporary work across several buildings. It is closed on Mondays, so check hours before you go; the Museum District is easy to reach by light rail.

signature.name: Houston Zoo
signature.detail: A major zoo in Hermann Park with thousands of animals and a strong reputation for family visits. Arrive at opening in the cooler morning hours, and note that the zoo sits next to the light rail line in the Museum District.

signature.name: Hermann Park
signature.detail: A large green space in the heart of the Museum District, home to the zoo, gardens and a lake, and a natural stop between nearby museums. Go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat; the park is served by the Metro light rail.

signature.name: Buffalo Bayou Park
signature.detail: A long stretch of trails, gardens and skyline views along the bayou just west of downtown, popular for walking and biking. Early morning or sunset gives the best light and cooler temperatures; rent a bike or walk in from nearby neighborhoods.

signature.name: The Galleria
signature.detail: Texas's best-known shopping destination, with hundreds of stores, dining and an indoor ice rink under one roof. It is busiest on weekends, so weekday mornings are calmer; parking is plentiful but rideshare avoids the garage hassle.

signature.name: Downtown Aquarium
signature.detail: An aquarium and entertainment complex downtown with exhibits and a Ferris wheel, good for families. Check exhibit hours before visiting and combine it with a walk around downtown; it is close to the theater district.

signature.name: Rice University
signature.detail: A handsome, walkable campus known for its architecture and tree-lined grounds in the Museum District. It is free to stroll; go on a weekday for a quieter visit and pair it with nearby Hermann Park.

signature.name: Charminar
signature.detail: The 16th-century four-minaret arch that is Hyderabad's defining icon and the heart of the old city. Go early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat and crowds, and dress modestly if you climb to the upper level. It sits right beside Laad Bazaar and Mecca Masjid, so you can see all three on foot.

signature.name: Golconda Fort
signature.detail: A vast hilltop fortress famous for its acoustics, ramparts and views over the city. Allow two to three hours for the climb and bring water and sun protection; the sound-and-light show in the evening is a popular add-on. It is a short taxi ride from the old city.

signature.name: Mecca Masjid
signature.detail: One of India's largest and oldest mosques, built under the Qutb Shahi rulers and standing next to Charminar. Visitors should cover shoulders and legs and remove shoes; non-Muslims can usually view the courtyard outside prayer times. Combine it with a walk through Laad Bazaar.

signature.name: Chowmahalla Palace
signature.detail: The elegant former seat of the Nizams, with courtyards, a clock tower and vintage car collections. It is a calm, well-kept stop near Charminar and takes about an hour; check opening days before you go as it closes on some weekdays.

signature.name: Salar Jung Museum
signature.detail: A huge, eclectic collection assembled by one family, from sculpture to clocks and manuscripts. It is a good indoor option in the afternoon heat and needs at least two hours; it sits across the river from the old city.

signature.name: Hussain Sagar Buddha statue
signature.detail: A giant standing Buddha on an island in Hussain Sagar Lake, best seen from the lakeside promenade or by boat. Sunset is the most comfortable time, and the Tank Bund road is an easy taxi or auto-rickshaw ride from the center.

signature.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
signature.detail: A quiet complex of domed royal tombs near Golconda Fort, among the best-preserved of their kind in India. Pair it with a Golconda visit since they are close together, and go in the cooler morning hours.

signature.name: Birla Mandir
signature.detail: A white marble Hindu temple on a hill with wide views over the city and lake. It is free to enter, shoes are left outside, and evenings are pleasant; it is a short ride from Hussain Sagar.

signature.name: Rawal Lake

signature.name: Istiqlal Mosque
signature.detail: Southeast Asia's largest mosque and a striking modern landmark right by Monas. Visitors can tour the prayer halls outside prayer times. Dress modestly and cover shoulders and legs; robes are often available at the entrance.

signature.name: Kota Tua Jakarta
signature.detail: The old Dutch colonial quarter with historic buildings, squares and museums, best explored on foot. Come in the morning or late afternoon for cooler weather and better light. It is easily reached by train to Jakarta Kota station.

signature.detail: This giant fountain shoots seawater high above the Red Sea and is Jeddah's best-known modern sight, especially dramatic after dark when it is lit. It is a quick, free stop rather than a long visit. Come at night for the best view from the Corniche; no tickets are needed.

signature.detail: A large scenic lake in the center of Jinan, ringed by gardens, temples and willow-lined paths, ideal for a relaxed half-day walk. Late afternoon is the best time for light and cooler temperatures; boats are available on site.

signature.name: Thousand Buddha Mountain
signature.detail: A hillside park with Buddhist carvings, temples and panoramic views over the city. Wear comfortable shoes for the climb and go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat.

signature.name: Soweto
signature.detail: The sprawling township is a living monument to South Africa's past and present, best explored with a local guide. Visit on a weekday morning for a calmer experience and to see daily life in action.

signature.name: Ponte City
signature.detail: This iconic cylindrical tower is a symbol of Johannesburg's urban renewal. While not generally open to the public, it's best viewed from nearby neighbourhoods or on a guided city tour.

signature.name: Maboneng Precinct

signature.name: Batu Caves

signature.detail: One of the largest Chinese temples in Southeast Asia, with ornate roofs and city views from its hillside setting. It is free to enter; dress modestly and visit in the morning for quieter grounds. A taxi or ride-hailing car is the easiest way up.

signature.name: Merdeka 118

signature.name: National Mosque of Malaysia
signature.detail: A striking modern mosque with a distinctive folded-roof design, open to visitors outside prayer times. Entry is free; dress code requires covered shoulders and legs, with robes often provided. It is a short walk from the Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia.

signature.detail: A bustling traditional market where you can experience old Kuwaiti commerce, spices, and local food. It's the heart of the city's heritage and a great place to wander. Tip: visit in the late afternoon or evening when it's liveliest; bargain politely and try the local snacks.

signature.name: Grand Mosque of Kuwait

signature.name: Tareq Rajab Museum

signature.name: Ljubljana Castle
signature.detail: The hilltop castle is the city's defining sight, with views over the old town and river. Walk up from the old town or take the funicular; go early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Triple Bridge
signature.detail: This trio of bridges by Jože Plečnik links the old town with the modern centre and is the city's most photographed spot. It is free and open at all hours, so visit at dusk when the riverside cafés light up.

signature.name: Prešeren Square
signature.detail: The main square is the heart of the old town, framed by the Franciscan church and the Triple Bridge. It is a natural starting point for a walking tour; mornings are calmest.

signature.name: St. Nicholas Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's main cathedral is known for its ornate baroque interior and bronze doors. It is free to enter outside service times; dress modestly and keep quiet during mass.

signature.name: Tivoli Park
signature.detail: Ljubljana's largest park offers wooded paths and a formal promenade leading up to the castle hill. It is free and ideal for a morning walk; enter from Prešeren Square via the Jakopič promenade.

signature.name: Metelkova Mesto
signature.detail: This former barracks turned autonomous art and culture zone is covered in murals and street art. Visit in daylight for photos and check what is on in the evening; it is a short walk from the centre.

signature.name: National Museum of Slovenia
signature.detail: The country's main museum holds archaeology and history collections, including the famous Ljubljana Marshes wheel. Check opening days before you go and allow a couple of hours.
