signature.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
signature.detail: The world's first Universal park and a must for movie fans, combining a working studio tour with major rides. Buy tickets online in advance and arrive at opening to beat the queues; it is in Universal City, reachable by Metro B Line.

signature.name: Hollywood Sign
signature.detail: The most recognizable symbol of the film industry, best seen from Griffith Park or the Lake Hollywood area. Go early in the morning for clear light and fewer crowds; there is no parking at the sign itself, so hike or view from a distance.

signature.name: Griffith Observatory
signature.detail: A free public observatory with sweeping views over Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign. Entry is free but planetarium shows are ticketed; visit at sunset for the best light and check opening days, as it is closed on some weekdays.

signature.name: Santa Monica Pier
signature.detail: A classic seaside pier with an amusement park, aquarium and ocean views at the end of Route 66. It is free to walk on; ride the Ferris wheel at sunset and take the Metro E Line to Downtown Santa Monica.

signature.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
signature.detail: The famous sidewalk of celebrity stars along Hollywood Boulevard, free to stroll. Come early or on a weekday to avoid crowds, and combine it with the TCL Chinese Theatre next door.

signature.name: The Getty Center
signature.detail: A hilltop art museum with world-class collections, gardens and panoramic city views. Admission is free; pay only for parking, and take the tram up from the garage.

signature.name: Venice Beach
signature.detail: A lively boardwalk with street performers, muscle beach and canals nearby. Rent a bike to ride to Santa Monica; weekends are busiest, so go on a weekday morning.

signature.name: TCL Chinese Theatre
signature.detail: Historic movie palace famous for its forecourt of celebrity handprints and footprints. The forecourt is free to visit; book a movie ticket to see the ornate interior.

signature.name: Grand Ducal Palace
signature.detail: The official residence of the Grand Duke and the ceremonial heart of the capital, set right in the old town. It is a must-see for its elegant facade and changing of the guard. Visit in summer when guided tours inside are offered; check times in advance.

signature.name: Bock Casemates
signature.detail: A vast network of underground tunnels carved into the cliffs, a UNESCO-listed highlight of the city's fortifications. The views over the valley are superb. Go early to avoid crowds and wear sturdy shoes for the uneven passages.

signature.name: Le Chemin de la Corniche
signature.detail: Known as Europe's most beautiful balcony, this walkway follows the old ramparts above the Grund valley. It is free and best at sunset for photos. Start near the Bock and stroll toward the city center.

signature.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral, Luxembourg
signature.detail: The city's main church, with a striking Gothic facade and a richly decorated interior. It is a calm stop in the old town and free to enter. Dress respectfully and visit on a weekday morning for quiet.

signature.name: Adolphe Bridge
signature.detail: The iconic arched bridge spanning the Pétrusse valley, a symbol of the city. Walk across for great views and photos. Combine it with a walk through the valley park below.

signature.name: Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière
signature.detail: Lyon's most famous sight, a hilltop basilica with sweeping views over the city and the Saône. It is a working religious site, so dress respectfully and keep quiet inside. Go early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds; you can walk up from Vieux Lyon or take the funicular.

signature.name: Vieux Lyon
signature.detail: One of Europe's largest Renaissance old towns, a maze of cobbled lanes and hidden passageways worth wandering for an afternoon. It sits at the foot of Fourvière, so pair the two in one outing. Come on a weekday to avoid the heaviest crowds.

signature.name: Traboules of Croix-Rousse
signature.detail: These covered passageways were used by silk workers and let you cut through buildings between streets. They are a distinctive Lyon experience and best explored on a guided walk, since some are private and closed to visitors. Wear comfortable shoes for the hills.

signature.name: Parc de la Tête d'Or
signature.detail: A large central park with a lake, gardens and a free botanical and zoo area, ideal for a relaxed break. It is free to enter and easy to reach by metro or bus. Visit in the morning for calm and cooler weather.

signature.name: Place Bellecour
signature.detail: A vast open square in the heart of the city, a natural meeting point between the two rivers and the old town. It is free and open at all hours. Use it as a landmark to orient yourself before heading to Vieux Lyon or the shops.

signature.name: Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste
signature.detail: A Gothic cathedral in Vieux Lyon with fine stained glass and an astronomical clock. Entry to the cathedral is generally free, though dress modestly. It is a short walk from the Saône and fits easily into an old-town stroll.

signature.name: Musée des Confluences
signature.detail: A striking modern museum at the meeting of the Rhône and Saône, covering natural history and world cultures. Its architecture alone is worth the trip. Check opening days and buy tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: Saône River Cruise
signature.detail: A boat trip on the Saône gives a different view of the old town and the hills. It is a good way to rest your feet after walking. Book a daytime departure and arrive a little early for a good seat.

signature.name: Prado Museum
signature.detail: Spain's premier art museum, home to masterpieces by Velázquez, Goya and El Greco. Book tickets online to skip the queue, and visit early morning or late afternoon for fewer crowds.

signature.name: Royal Palace of Madrid
signature.detail: The official residence of the Spanish royal family, with over 3,000 opulent rooms. Arrive early to avoid long lines, and check for changing of the guard schedules.

signature.name: Plaza Mayor
signature.detail: A grand 17th-century square surrounded by arcades and historic buildings. Best visited in the evening when the lights come on; it's a short walk from Puerta del Sol.

signature.name: Retiro Park
signature.detail: Madrid's most beloved park, featuring a tranquil lake and the Crystal Palace. Rent a rowboat or simply stroll; it's easily reached by metro at Retiro station.

signature.name: Reina Sofia Museum
signature.detail: Home to Picasso's Guernica and an outstanding collection of modern Spanish art. Free entry during certain hours; go early or late to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Puerta del Sol
signature.detail: The bustling heart of Madrid, famous for its clock tower and the 'Oso y el Madroño' statue. Visit at night to see the illuminated neon signs and enjoy people-watching.

signature.name: Temple of Debod
signature.detail: An ancient Egyptian temple gifted to Spain, set in a scenic park with stunning sunset views. Free to visit; go at dusk for the best photos.

signature.name: Gran Vía
signature.detail: Madrid's most famous shopping street, lined with grand architecture and theaters. Best explored on foot; it's a short walk from Puerta del Sol.

signature.name: Puerto Salvador Allende
signature.detail: Managua's lakeside urban hub and the city's best-known gathering spot, with restaurants, a boardwalk and views over Lake Xolotlán. Go in the late afternoon for cooler air and sunset over the water; it's a short taxi ride from the center and best avoided after dark.

signature.name: Old Cathedral of Managua
signature.detail: The earthquake-ruined shell of the old cathedral is Managua's most striking historic sight and a symbol of the 1972 quake. View it from the plaza outside; it is not open for regular visits, so plan a quick photo stop rather than a tour inside.

signature.name: Loma de Tiscapa
signature.detail: A hilltop park with the giant Sandino silhouette statue and sweeping views across the city and lake. Come in the morning for clearer skies and cooler temperatures, and take a taxi up rather than walking.

signature.name: National Palace of Culture, Managua
signature.detail: A handsome historic building on the Plaza de la Revolución housing museums and murals. Check opening hours before you go, as they can be limited, and combine it with a walk around the plaza.

signature.name: National Museum of Nicaragua
signature.detail: The country's main museum, with archaeology, history and art exhibits that give context to the city. Allow an hour or two and confirm opening days, which vary.

signature.name: Paseo Xolotlán
signature.detail: A lakeside promenade with sculptures, small attractions and lake views, popular with local families. Visit in the early evening and stick to the busier sections.

signature.name: Masaya Artisan Market
signature.detail: A market known for crafts, hammocks and souvenirs, useful for gifts. Bring small bills and be ready to bargain politely; it's best reached by taxi or as part of a day trip toward Masaya.

signature.name: Bahrain Fort
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this sprawling 16th-century Portuguese fort sits atop the ancient Dilmun capital of Qal'at al-Bahrain, offering sweeping views and layers of history. signature.name: Al Fateh Grand Mosque
signature.detail: One of the world's largest mosques, it welcomes non-Muslim visitors and boasts a stunning fiberglass dome and intricate Islamic calligraphy. signature.detail: The home of Manchester United and one of the most famous football stadiums in the world, a pilgrimage for fans. Take a stadium tour to see the dressing rooms and tunnel; book tickets in advance, especially on match weekends.

signature.name: Science and Industry Museum
signature.detail: Housed in the world's oldest surviving passenger railway station, it tells the story of Manchester's industrial revolution. Entry is free; go on a weekday morning to avoid school groups.

signature.name: Manchester Art Gallery
signature.detail: A strong collection of fine art and decorative arts in a grand Victorian building. Free entry; combine with a stroll through the nearby Chinatown or Piccadilly Gardens.

signature.name: John Rylands Library
signature.detail: A stunning neo-Gothic library that looks like a cathedral for books, home to rare manuscripts. Free to enter; it's a quiet spot, so visit early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Chetham's Library
signature.detail: The oldest public library in the English-speaking world, dating from 1653, and a hidden gem. Entry is by guided tour only; check times and book ahead.

signature.name: Manchester Cathedral
signature.detail: A beautiful medieval church with a striking modern extension, right in the city centre. Free to enter; open daily, but check for service times if you want to look around quietly.

signature.name: Castlefield
signature.detail: A historic area with Roman ruins and canal-side walks, now a trendy spot with bars and restaurants. Best explored on foot; start at the Roman gardens and follow the canal.

signature.name: Etihad Stadium
signature.detail: Home of Manchester City, a modern football stadium with tours available. Take the tram to Etihad Campus; tours run most days but check availability online.

signature.name: Royal Exchange Theatre
signature.detail: A unique theatre-in-the-round inside the historic Royal Exchange building. Catch a show if you can; otherwise, the building is worth a look for its architecture.

signature.name: University of Manchester
signature.detail: A leading university with a notable campus and museums like the Manchester Museum. Wander the campus and visit the free Manchester Museum; it's a short bus ride from the centre.

signature.name: Fort Santiago

signature.name: San Agustin Church
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed baroque church and the oldest stone church in the Philippines. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) and visit outside mass times for quiet viewing.

signature.name: Rizal Park
signature.detail: A large urban park honoring national hero José Rizal, with gardens and monuments. Best visited in the late afternoon when locals gather; it's a short walk from Intramuros.

signature.detail: Marseille's most famous sight, a hilltop basilica crowned by a golden statue of the Virgin that watches over the whole city and the sea. signature.name: Calanques National Park
signature.detail: A dramatic stretch of limestone coves and turquoise water right at the city's edge, the reason many people fall in love with Marseille. signature.name: MuCEM
signature.detail: A striking modern museum on the waterfront, linked to the old Fort Saint-Jean by footbridges, devoted to Mediterranean cultures. signature.name: Cathédrale de la Major
signature.detail: A vast, striped Romanesque-Byzantine cathedral near the port, far bigger and more ornate than most visitors expect. It sits beside the MuCEM and the Joliette district, so it fits easily into a waterfront walk. Entry is free; dress respectfully and avoid visiting during services.

signature.name: Palais Longchamp
signature.detail: A grand 19th-century palace built around a monumental water fountain, with gardens and museums on either side. It is a favorite spot for a relaxed stroll away from the port crowds. Come in the morning for quiet gardens, and check museum opening days before planning a visit.

signature.name: Orange Velodrome
signature.detail: Marseille's iconic football stadium, home of Olympique de Marseille and famous for its roaring atmosphere on match days. Even outside games, it is a landmark of the city's sporting identity. Tickets for matches sell fast, so book well ahead and arrive early for the walk from the metro.

signature.name: Royal Exhibition Building
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the world's oldest surviving exhibition halls, it is the grand centrepiece of Carlton Gardens. signature.name: Flinders Street Station
signature.detail: The city's most photographed facade, a yellow Edwardian landmark sitting right on the Yarra at the main rail hub. It is free to admire from the corner of Swanston and Flinders Streets; come at dusk when the clocks and dome light up.

signature.name: Shrine of Remembrance
signature.detail: Victoria's solemn war memorial, with a crypt, gallery and a rooftop balcony giving sweeping views over the city. Entry is free; it is a short walk from the Royal Botanic Gardens and best visited in the cooler morning hours.

signature.name: Federation Square
signature.detail: The city's central urban hub, home to major museums and galleries and a natural meeting point by the river. Drop by for the architecture and events, then walk across to the Yarra for the riverside promenade.

signature.name: National Gallery of Victoria
signature.detail: Australia's oldest and most visited public gallery, with a strong international and Australian collection and a famous stained-glass ceiling. General entry is free; allow a few hours and check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Queen Victoria Market
signature.detail: A sprawling historic market for produce, deli goods and souvenirs, and a Melbourne institution. Go early in the morning for the freshest food and fewer crowds; it is a short tram ride from the central grid.

signature.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
signature.detail: One of the world's great sports stadiums and the spiritual home of Australian cricket and football. Book a stadium tour or catch a match; the surrounding parkland is an easy walk from the city.

signature.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
signature.detail: Lush, free gardens along the river with lakes, lawns and themed plant collections. Enter from the Shrine side and bring water and sun protection; it is ideal for a relaxed half-day.

signature.name: Eureka Tower
signature.detail: A soaring skyscraper whose Skydeck offers the best high views over the city and bay. Go near sunset for day-to-night views, and book tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: St Kilda Beach
signature.detail: The city's classic seaside escape, with a pier, promenade and nearby penguin viewing at dusk. Take a tram from the centre and allow time to wander the foreshore.

signature.name: South Beach
signature.detail: Miami's most famous stretch of sand, known for its turquoise water, lively boardwalk and people-watching. Go early in the morning for a quieter beach and cooler sun, and bring your own towel and water since rentals add up.

signature.name: Art Deco Historic District
signature.detail: A compact stretch of pastel 1920s-30s buildings along Ocean Drive and Collins Avenue, best explored on foot. Late afternoon light is ideal for photos, and many buildings are best appreciated from the street.

signature.name: Wynwood Walls
signature.detail: An open-air gallery of large-scale street murals that changes regularly and anchors the Wynwood arts neighborhood. Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and wear comfortable shoes for walking the surrounding blocks.

signature.name: Little Havana
signature.detail: The heart of Miami's Cuban community, centered on Calle Ocho with cigar shops, cafes and street life. Go in the afternoon for the liveliest atmosphere and expect to pay in cash at smaller spots.

signature.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
signature.detail: A grand waterfront estate with formal gardens and richly decorated interiors, one of Miami's most photogenic sights. Book tickets online in advance and go at opening time to beat the heat and crowds.

signature.name: Everglades National Park
signature.detail: A vast wetland wilderness just outside the city, home to alligators, wading birds and mangrove channels. Start early, bring insect repellent and sun protection, and check the park entrance and tour options before you go.

signature.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
signature.detail: A waterfront modern and contemporary art museum with strong holdings of Latin American and Caribbean work. It is a good indoor option on hot or rainy days; check opening days and ticket prices online.

signature.name: Miami Beach
signature.detail: The barrier island that holds South Beach and much of the city's beach culture, with a long oceanfront promenade. Use the public beach access points and arrive before midday for parking and space.

signature.detail: Milan's cathedral is the city's defining icon, with a vast marble facade and a rooftop terrace of spires and statues. Book rooftop tickets online in advance and go early morning to beat the crowds; dress modestly as it is a working church.

signature.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
signature.detail: This grand 19th-century glass-roofed arcade links the Duomo to Teatro alla Scala and is a must-see for its mosaics and architecture. It is free to walk through; visit early or late to avoid the busiest crowds.

signature.name: Sforza Castle

signature.name: Piazza del Duomo
signature.detail: The central square is the natural starting point for any Milan visit, framed by the cathedral and the Galleria. It is open at all hours and free; arrive early for the calmest photos.

signature.name: Minneapolis Institute of Art
signature.detail: One of the finest encyclopedic art museums in the country, with a vast collection spanning centuries and cultures. Admission is free, so it is an easy must-see; go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Minneapolis Sculpture Garden
signature.detail: Home to the iconic Spoonbridge and Cherry, this garden is a beloved photo spot and a relaxing green space. Visit in the late afternoon for softer light; it is free and open daily.

signature.name: Stone Arch Bridge
signature.detail: A historic stone bridge offering stunning views of the Mississippi River and the city skyline. Walk or bike across at sunset for the best photos; it is free and accessible from downtown.

signature.name: Minnehaha Falls
signature.detail: A beautiful 53-foot waterfall in a city park, perfect for a nature escape without leaving Minneapolis. Go after rain for a stronger flow; the park is free and has walking trails.

signature.name: Mall of America
signature.detail: The largest shopping mall in the US, featuring an amusement park, aquarium, and hundreds of stores. It is a must-see for entertainment; arrive early on weekends to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Walker Art Center
signature.detail: A contemporary art museum known for its innovative exhibitions and adjacent sculpture garden. Check for free admission days; the museum is a short walk from the Sculpture Garden.

signature.name: Target Field
signature.detail: A modern baseball stadium in downtown Minneapolis, home to the Minnesota Twins. Catch a game for the lively atmosphere; tickets are affordable and the stadium is easily reached by light rail.

signature.name: University of Minnesota Twin Cities
signature.detail: A major public university with a vibrant campus and cultural events. Explore the Weisman Art Museum and stroll the campus; it is free to visit and well-connected by transit.

signature.name: Macroplaza
signature.detail: Monterrey's vast central plaza is the city's urban heart and the natural starting point for a first visit, linking the old town with the modern downtown. Go in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat, and wear comfortable shoes for the long walk across it.

signature.name: Cerro de la Silla
signature.detail: The saddle-shaped mountain is Monterrey's defining icon and frames the city from almost everywhere. The best views are on clear mornings; head to a viewpoint or the surrounding hills rather than attempting the summit without proper gear.

signature.name: Parque Fundidora
signature.detail: A former steelworks turned sprawling park, it blends industrial heritage with green space and is a favorite for a relaxed half-day. Visit early on weekends to beat the crowds, and bring water and sun protection as shade is limited in parts.

signature.name: Barrio Antiguo
signature.detail: The cobblestone old quarter is the most atmospheric place to wander, with colorful facades and a lively evening scene. Come in the late afternoon for photos, then stay for dinner; it is easily reached on foot from the Macroplaza.

signature.name: Museo de Historia Mexicana
signature.detail: A well-regarded museum tracing Mexican history, located right by the Macroplaza and worth an air-conditioned break from the heat. Check opening days before you go, as many museums close on Mondays.

signature.name: Palacio Salvo
signature.detail: This landmark palace towers over Plaza Independencia and is Montevideo's most recognizable silhouette. Check opening hours before going up for views, and pair it with a walk around the plaza.

signature.name: Plaza Independencia
signature.detail: The main square links the old town with the modern city and is the natural starting point for sightseeing. Visit in the morning or early evening; it is an easy walk from Ciudad Vieja.

signature.name: Teatro Solis
signature.detail: One of South America's grand old theaters, worth seeing for its architecture and performances. Book tickets or a guided visit in advance, and dress smartly for evening shows.

signature.name: Rambla de Montevideo
signature.detail: The long waterfront promenade is where locals walk, run and watch the sunset over the river. Go late afternoon for the best light; it is free and easy to reach from most of the city.

signature.name: Mercado del Puerto

signature.name: Old Montreal
signature.detail: The historic heart of the city, with cobblestone streets, 18th-century architecture, and a lively waterfront. Wander on foot and stop at Place Jacques-Cartier; best explored in the morning before tour groups arrive.

signature.name: Saint Joseph's Oratory
signature.detail: Canada's largest church, perched on Mount Royal, draws pilgrims and visitors for its impressive dome and city views. Entry to the basilica is free; take the metro to Côte-des-Neiges and wear comfortable shoes for the climb.

signature.name: Mount Royal Park
signature.detail: Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, this sprawling park offers the best skyline views from the Kondiaronk Belvedere. Go at sunset for a spectacular panorama; it's a short walk from downtown or a quick bus ride.

signature.name: Place Jacques-Cartier
signature.detail: A lively public square in Old Montreal, lined with street performers, cafés, and historic buildings. It's perfect for people-watching; visit in summer when the square is buzzing with activity.

signature.name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
signature.detail: One of Canada's most prestigious art museums, with an encyclopedic collection spanning centuries. Check for free admission to the permanent collection on the first Sunday of each month; the museum is easily reached by metro at Guy-Concordia.

signature.name: Jean-Talon Market
signature.detail: One of North America's largest open-air markets, bursting with fresh produce, local cheeses, and artisanal goods. Go hungry and sample the stalls; it's a short walk from Jean-Talon metro station and best visited on weekday mornings.

signature.name: Olympic Park and Biodome
signature.detail: Built for the 1976 Olympics, this complex includes the iconic inclined tower and the Biodome's immersive ecosystems. Buy a combined ticket for the Biodome and tower; take metro line 1 to Pie-IX and allow at least half a day.

signature.name: Red Square
signature.detail: The vast cobblestone heart of Moscow, ringed by the Kremlin, St. Basil's and GUM, and the first place every visitor heads. Come early morning or after dark to dodge the crowds and catch the buildings lit up. It's free and open around the clock; the nearest metro is Okhotny Ryad.

signature.name: Moscow Kremlin
signature.detail: A walled city of cathedrals, palaces and armouries that has been the seat of Russian power for centuries. Buy tickets online and go on a weekday morning; the Armoury Chamber needs a separate timed ticket. Enter from the Alexander Garden side via metro Biblioteka imeni Lenina.

signature.name: St. Basil's Cathedral
signature.detail: The candy-coloured onion domes on Red Square are Russia's most recognisable silhouette. Step inside to see the maze of chapels, and photograph it from the Zaryadye Park side at sunset. Tickets are sold at the door; modest dress is respectful.

signature.name: Lenin's Mausoleum
signature.detail: A starkly modern tomb on Red Square holding the embalmed body of the Soviet founder. It's free but opens only a few short morning hours and closes on some weekdays, so check ahead; no bags, phones or photos inside, and expect a queue.

signature.name: Tretyakov Gallery
signature.detail: The definitive collection of Russian painting, from medieval icons to the Blue Dancers and the great 19th-century masters. Allow at least half a day and book a timed ticket online to skip the line. Metro Tretyakovskaya is right outside.

signature.name: GUM
signature.detail: The elegant 19th-century arcade facing the Kremlin, now a department store with a glass roof and historic cafés. It's a good rain shelter and a classic photo spot; go in the evening when the facade is illuminated. Metro Ploshchad Revolyutsii.

signature.name: Moscow Metro Stations
signature.detail: Moscow's underground palaces — chandeliers, mosaics and marble — are a sight in themselves and the cheapest way to cross the city. Ride the circle line and stop at Komsomolskaya and Novoslobodskaya; avoid rush hour for photos. A single trip costs a few dollars.

signature.name: Bolshoi Theatre
signature.detail: One of the world's great opera and ballet houses, with a gilded auditorium that alone justifies the visit. Book ballet or opera tickets well in advance online, or take a guided backstage tour if performances are sold out. Metro Teatralnaya.

signature.name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour
signature.detail: A colossal white-and-gold cathedral rebuilt in the 1990s, dominating the Moskva River bank near the Kremlin. Go up to the viewing gallery for river views and dress modestly; entry to the main church is free. Metro Kropotkinskaya.

signature.name: Novodevichy Convent
signature.detail: A serene walled convent with red-and-white towers and a famous cemetery of Russian artists and leaders next door. It's a peaceful half-day away from the centre; combine it with a walk around the pond. Metro Sportivnaya.

signature.name: Gateway of India
signature.detail: Mumbai's most famous monument, a basalt arch on the harborfront built to commemorate a royal visit. Go early morning to avoid crowds and heat; it's free and a short walk from Colaba Causeway.

signature.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic railway station that is still a working commuter hub. Visit outside rush hours (mid-morning or afternoon) to admire the facade and interior without the crush; it's free to enter.

signature.name: Elephanta Caves
signature.detail: Ancient rock-cut cave temples on an island in Mumbai Harbour, reached by a one-hour ferry from the Gateway of India. Ferries run roughly 9am–2pm and are closed on Mondays; wear comfortable shoes for the climb.

signature.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
signature.detail: Mumbai's iconic heritage hotel facing the Gateway of India, famed for its architecture and history. Non-guests can visit the lobby and some restaurants; dress smart-casual and expect security checks.

signature.name: Marine Drive
signature.detail: The sweeping seaside promenade known as the Queen's Necklace, best at sunset when the lights come on. It's free and ideal for an evening stroll; avoid midday heat.

signature.name: Haji Ali Dargah
signature.detail: A mosque and tomb on an islet linked by a causeway, a striking sight at high tide. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees); it's free and busiest on Fridays.

signature.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
signature.detail: One of Mumbai's most visited Hindu temples, dedicated to Ganesha. Remove shoes and dress respectfully; early morning or late evening is less crowded, and it's free to enter.

signature.name: Dhobi Ghat
signature.detail: A vast open-air laundry where dhobis wash clothes by hand, a unique slice of Mumbai life. View from the Mahalaxmi bridge for free; be respectful and ask before photographing workers.

food: About $38 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $58 a night for two
transport: About $6 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Marienplatz
signature.detail: Munich's central square is the beating heart of the old town and the natural starting point for any first visit. Arrive a few minutes before the hour to watch the Glockenspiel figures in the Neues Rathaus tower re-enact a wedding and a barrel-maker's dance. It is a short walk from Marienplatz U-Bahn/S-Bahn station, and mornings are quieter than midday.

signature.name: Nymphenburg Palace
signature.detail: The sprawling baroque summer residence of the former Bavarian rulers, with a grand central pavilion and long formal gardens. Allow at least half a day to see the palace rooms and stroll the park pavilions. Take tram 17 to the Schloss Nymphenburg stop and buy a combined ticket if you plan to enter the pavilions.

signature.name: English Garden
signature.detail: One of the world's largest urban parks, with meadows, river surfers at the Eisbach wave and traditional beer gardens under the chestnut trees. It is free and open at all hours, so go early for calm paths or late afternoon for the liveliest atmosphere. The Chinesischer Turm beer garden is a good central rest stop.

signature.name: Munich Residenz
signature.detail: The former royal palace of the Wittelsbachs, a vast complex of courtyards, state rooms and the treasury filled with crown jewels and silver. The Antiquarium alone is worth the visit. It sits right by Marienplatz, so pair it with the old town; buy a combined ticket for the museum and treasury.

signature.name: Neues Rathaus
signature.detail: The neo-Gothic city hall dominates Marienplatz with its ornate facade and famous clock tower. Climb the tower lift for a close-up view over the square and rooftops. Go up shortly before the hour to see the Glockenspiel from above, and note the tower has a small entry fee.

signature.name: Allianz Arena
signature.detail: The glowing, cushion-shaped stadium home to Bayern Munich and a landmark of modern Munich architecture. Take a guided stadium tour or catch a match if your dates align; the arena is a short U-Bahn ride from the centre. Check the tour schedule ahead, as match days close the stadium to visitors.

food: About $53 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $200 a night for two
transport: About $21 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
signature.detail: Oman's most impressive modern mosque, with a vast prayer hall, a huge hand-knotted carpet and a chandelier that draw visitors from across the region. Non-Muslims may visit in the morning on most days; dress modestly with covered arms, legs and hair for women, and arrive early to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Royal Opera House Muscat
signature.detail: A striking marble-and-wood opera house that is the cultural centerpiece of the city, worth seeing even outside performance times. Guided tours run on selected mornings; book ahead and check the schedule, as access depends on rehearsals.

signature.name: Al Alam Palace
signature.detail: The ceremonial palace of the Sultan, framed by distinctive blue and gold columns and set between two old forts. You cannot enter, but the exterior and surrounding plaza are a classic photo stop; go in the cooler early morning or late afternoon.

signature.name: Muttrah Souq
signature.detail: A maze of old lanes selling frankincense, silver, textiles and spices, one of the most atmospheric markets in the Gulf. Visit in the evening when it is liveliest and cooler, and bargain politely.

signature.name: Mutrah Corniche
signature.detail: A long waterfront promenade curving past the harbor, with views of the forts and the palace beyond. Best walked at sunset or early evening; it is free and connects easily to the souq.

signature.name: Qurum Beach
signature.detail: A broad sandy beach popular with locals for evening walks and picnics. Go late afternoon for cooler air; swimming is fine but check local advice and dress modestly away from the sand.

signature.name: Bait Al Zubair
signature.detail: A private museum of Omani heritage with costumes, weapons, jewelry and a reconstructed traditional house. A good introduction to local culture; check opening hours, as they vary by day and season.

signature.name: Al Jalali & Al Mirani Forts
signature.detail: Twin Portuguese-era forts guarding the harbor, seen best from the corniche and souq area. They are generally not open for interior visits, so plan them as a viewpoint and photo stop rather than a tour.

food: Casual meal $5-12; mid-range dinner $15-30
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $80-140 a night
transport: Taxis and ride-hailing $3-10 a trip; car hire about $30-50 a day

signature.name: Nairobi National Park
signature.detail: The only national park inside a capital city, where you can see lions, rhinos and giraffes against a skyline backdrop. Go early morning for the best wildlife sightings and cooler temperatures; arrange a guided game drive or self-drive with a 4x4.

signature.name: Giraffe Centre
signature.detail: A conservation centre where you can hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes from a raised platform. Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds; tickets are available at the gate and include a short educational talk.

signature.name: Karen Blixen Museum
signature.detail: The former home of the author of 'Out of Africa', preserved with original furnishings and lush gardens. Take a guided tour for context; it's a short drive from the Giraffe Centre, so combine both in one trip.

signature.name: Nairobi National Museum
signature.detail: Kenya's flagship museum, covering human origins, ethnography and natural history, including the famous Turkana Boy fossil. Allow at least two hours; it's centrally located and easily reached by taxi.

signature.name: Kenyatta International Convention Centre
signature.detail: An iconic tower with a rooftop helipad offering panoramic views of Nairobi. Go on a clear day for the best photos; the observation deck is open to visitors for a small fee.

signature.name: Karura Forest
signature.detail: A serene urban forest with walking and cycling trails, waterfalls and caves. Rent a bike at the entrance or join a guided walk; go early to avoid the heat and bring water.

signature.name: Bomas of Kenya
signature.detail: A cultural village showcasing traditional homesteads and dance performances from Kenya's ethnic groups. Check the performance schedule in advance; it's a short drive from the city centre.

signature.name: Ngong Hills
signature.detail: A scenic ridge offering hiking trails and sweeping views over the Rift Valley. Arrange a guided hike for safety; start early and bring sun protection and water.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $24 a night for two

signature.name: Tengwang Pavilion
signature.detail: Nanchang's most famous ancient site and a must-see for its striking architecture and riverside views. Visit in the late afternoon to catch the sunset over the Gan River; entry is ticketed, so check hours in advance.

signature.name: Bayi Square
signature.detail: A vast historical square that commemorates the 1927 Nanchang Uprising and is a central gathering place. It's free and open all day; go in the evening to see the monument lit up.

signature.name: Meiling National Forest Park
signature.detail: A mountain escape just outside the city, ideal for hiking and enjoying nature. Best visited in spring or autumn; bring comfortable shoes and allow a full day.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $42 a night for two

signature.name: Dr. Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum
signature.detail: The resting place of modern China's founding father, set at the top of a grand 392-step stairway on Purple Mountain. It is the city's most iconic sight and draws huge crowds. Go early in the morning to beat the queues, and note the site is free but closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Confucius Temple, Nanjing
signature.detail: A restored temple and lively pedestrian quarter along the Qinhuai River, best known for its evening lights and boat rides. Come after dark when the lanterns are on, and combine it with a stroll through the surrounding snack streets.

signature.name: Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall
signature.detail: A sobering, deeply moving museum documenting the 1937 massacre, with powerful exhibits and architecture. It is free to enter but closed on Mondays; allow two hours and dress respectfully.

signature.name: Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum
signature.detail: The tomb of the first Ming emperor, reached along a beautiful spirit way lined with stone animals. It sits on Purple Mountain and pairs naturally with the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum; a combined scenic-area ticket saves money.

signature.name: Nanjing City Wall
signature.detail: One of the best-preserved ancient city walls in China, with walkable stretches and views over the old town and lakes. Walk a section near Zhonghua Gate in the late afternoon for cooler weather and good light.

signature.name: Presidential Palace
signature.detail: A sprawling complex of gardens and government buildings that witnessed key moments of modern Chinese history. It is central and easy to reach by metro; book ahead online as tickets sell out on weekends.

signature.name: Purple Mountain
signature.detail: The wooded mountain that anchors eastern Nanjing, dotted with tombs, temples and trails. Take the cable car or a taxi up, and set aside a full day to combine several sights on its slopes.

signature.name: Nanjing Museum
signature.detail: One of China's largest and finest museums, with strong collections of art, history and porcelain. Entry is free with advance reservation, and it is closed on Mondays.

food: About $52 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $100 a night for two
transport: About $41 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
signature.detail: The definitive museum of country music, with gold records, stage costumes and instruments from the genre's biggest stars. Book tickets online in advance and allow at least two to three hours; it sits downtown near the honky-tonks.

signature.name: Ryman Auditorium
signature.detail: The historic former home of the Grand Ole Opry, famed for its acoustics and pew seating. Check the schedule for concerts or take a daytime tour; it is a short walk from Broadway.

signature.name: Grand Ole Opry
signature.detail: The long-running live country music radio show and a Nashville institution. Shows are at the Opry House outside downtown, so plan transport and buy tickets well ahead.

signature.name: Johnny Cash Museum
signature.detail: A compact downtown museum devoted to the Man in Black, with memorabilia and personal items. It is popular and small, so go early in the day to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Belle Meade Historic Site
signature.detail: A preserved plantation estate with a mansion, grounds and a winery, offering a window into the region's history. It is a drive from downtown, so allow half a day and check tour times.

signature.name: Cheekwood Estate & Gardens
signature.detail: A botanical garden and art estate with seasonal displays and a historic mansion. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit; it is south of downtown and easiest by car.

signature.name: Vanderbilt University
signature.detail: A well-known university campus with leafy grounds near the city center. It is a pleasant walk-through stop, especially combined with nearby neighborhoods.

signature.name: Red Fort
signature.detail: The Mughal emperor's red sandstone fortress and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the setting for India's Independence Day address. Go early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds, and note that foreign visitors pay a higher ticket than locals.

signature.name: Qutub Minar
signature.detail: A soaring 73-metre victory tower from the 12th century, the tallest brick minaret in the world, surrounded by early Indo-Islamic tombs. Visit in the late afternoon for softer light; it is a short ride south of central Delhi.

signature.name: India Gate
signature.detail: The grand war memorial arch at the end of Rajpath, best seen lit up after dark when locals gather on the lawns. Come in the evening; there is no entry fee for the surrounding area.

signature.name: Humayun's Tomb
signature.detail: The garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal, a serene UNESCO-listed Mughal monument. Go at opening time for quiet paths and good photos; tickets are sold at the gate.

signature.name: Lotus Temple
signature.detail: A striking flower-shaped Bahai house of worship open to all faiths, known for its calm silent hall. Entry is free but you must remove your shoes and keep quiet inside; it is closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Buyuk Han
signature.detail: The best-preserved Ottoman caravanserai on the island, a peaceful courtyard of arched rooms right in the old town. It is the most atmospheric stop in Nicosia and easy to combine with the nearby bazaar. Go in the morning for quiet courtyards, and remember it is a historic site, so dress respectfully.

signature.name: Selimiye Mosque, Nicosia
signature.detail: A former Gothic cathedral turned mosque, it is the landmark of the old city and a striking mix of Christian and Islamic architecture. Visit outside prayer times, cover shoulders and knees, and remove shoes before entering. It sits a short walk from Buyuk Han, so pair the two.

signature.name: Cyprus Museum
signature.detail: The country's main archaeological museum, holding finds from across the island and essential context before exploring further. Allow a couple of hours and check opening hours, as it closes on some public holidays. It is a short walk from the old town walls.

signature.name: Ledra Street crossing
signature.detail: The best-known pedestrian crossing between the Greek and Turkish sides of the divided capital, a must for understanding modern Nicosia. Bring your passport for the checkpoint and go on foot during daytime hours. The street itself is lively with shops and cafes.

signature.name: Omeriye Mosque
signature.detail: A historic mosque in the old town, converted from a church and still an active place of worship. It is a quiet, worthwhile stop near the bazaar. Dress modestly and avoid visiting during prayer times.

signature.name: Famagusta Gate
signature.detail: One of the old Venetian gates through the city walls, now used as a cultural venue. It is a good landmark for understanding the star-shaped fortifications. Visit in daylight and combine it with a walk along the walls.

signature.name: Tianyi Pavilion
signature.detail: China's oldest surviving private library and the pride of Ningbo, a quiet garden complex of wooden halls and stone courtyards. It is the one sight first-time visitors come for. Go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and check opening hours before you set out as they can change by season.

signature.name: Osaka Castle
signature.detail: The city's defining landmark, with a reconstructed keep, moats and parkland that tell Osaka's story from the 16th century. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds, and note the castle museum charges an admission fee.

signature.name: Dotonbori
signature.detail: Osaka's neon-lit entertainment hub, famous for its canal-side signs and street-food stalls. Come after dark for the full effect, and arrive by metro to Namba station.

signature.name: Umeda Sky Building
signature.detail: A striking twin-tower complex with a floating garden observatory offering sweeping city views. Visit near sunset for the best light; there is a ticket for the observatory.

signature.name: Tsutenkaku
signature.detail: The retro tower that anchors the Shinsekai district, a beloved symbol of old Osaka. Combine it with a wander through Shinsekai's streets, and buy a ticket for the observation deck.

signature.name: Shitenno-ji
signature.detail: One of Japan's oldest Buddhist temples, with a peaceful precinct and a five-story pagoda. It is easily reached by metro and is calmest in the early morning.

signature.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha
signature.detail: A major shrine with distinctive architecture and a serene, wooded setting. Go in the morning for quiet, and check the shrine's own access from the nearby tram or train station.

signature.name: Universal Studios Japan
signature.detail: A major theme park and a big draw for first-time visitors, especially families. Book tickets in advance and arrive at opening to make the most of the day.

signature.name: Vigeland Park
signature.detail: A sprawling park filled with more than 200 sculptures by Gustav Vigeland, including the famous Monolith and Sinnataggen. It is free and open year-round; go early in the morning to avoid crowds, and take tram 12 to Vigelandsparken.

signature.name: Akershus Fortress
signature.detail: A medieval castle and fortress overlooking the Oslofjord, with grounds that are free to wander and a museum inside. Visit on a clear day for harbor views; the grounds are open daily, but check castle opening hours before you go.

signature.name: Oslo Opera House
signature.detail: A striking modern building you can walk on, with a marble roof sloping into the fjord. It is a must-see for architecture lovers; the roof is free to access, and guided tours of the interior are available if you book ahead.

signature.name: Viking Ship Museum, Oslo
signature.detail: Home to three remarkably preserved Viking ships and burial treasures from the 9th century. Note that the museum is closed for renovation until 2026/2027, so check the official website before planning your visit.

signature.name: Munch Museum
signature.detail: A towering museum dedicated to Edvard Munch, housing versions of The Scream and thousands of other works. It is a must for art fans; book tickets online and allow at least two hours, and consider a combined ticket with other museums.

signature.name: The Royal Palace
signature.detail: The official residence of the Norwegian monarch, set in a pleasant park with daily changing of the guard. The park is free to visit; guided tours of the palace interior run in summer and must be booked in advance.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $152 a night for two

signature.name: Panama Canal
signature.detail: The engineering marvel that made Panama famous, where ships rise and fall through the locks in a matter of minutes. The Miraflores Locks are the classic viewing spot, and ships are most frequent in the morning, so arrive early and check the day's transit schedule before you go.

signature.name: Casco Viejo
signature.detail: The restored colonial old town is the city's most atmospheric quarter, with plazas, churches and rooftop bars on the water's edge. Come in the late afternoon to walk the streets in cooler light, then stay for dinner; it is easily reached by taxi or rideshare from the modern center.

signature.name: Panama Viejo
signature.detail: The stone ruins of the original Spanish settlement are a UNESCO-listed archaeological site and a reminder of the city's violent colonial history. It is an open, sunny site with little shade, so bring water and a hat and go in the morning.

signature.name: BioMuseo
signature.detail: Frank Gehry's colorful museum tells the story of Panama's extraordinary biodiversity and is a striking piece of architecture in its own right. It sits on the Amador Causeway, so combine it with a walk or bike ride along the waterfront; buy tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: Bridge of the Americas
signature.detail: The great arch spanning the canal at the Pacific entrance is a landmark of modern Panama and a favorite photo stop. It is best seen from the Amador Causeway at sunset, when the bridge and the canal traffic light up.

food: About $36 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $70 a night for two

signature.name: Fremantle Prison
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of Australia's most intact convict-era prisons, with guided tours through cell blocks and tunnels. Book a tour in advance, as the popular tunnel and night tours sell out; it is a short train ride from central Perth to Fremantle.

signature.name: Elizabeth Quay
signature.detail: The waterfront hub on the Swan River, with the Swan Bell Tower nearby and easy access to ferries and riverside walks. Visit in the late afternoon for sunset over the river; it is walkable from the CBD or reachable by train to Elizabeth Quay station.

signature.name: Cottesloe Beach
signature.detail: Perth's classic white-sand beach, great for swimming and sunset views over the Indian Ocean. Go early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat and crowds; the train to Cottesloe station puts you a short walk from the sand.

signature.name: Kings Park and Botanic Garden
signature.detail: A vast park overlooking the city and Swan River, with native botanic gardens and sweeping skyline views. It is free to enter and best explored in the cooler morning hours; it is a short walk or bus ride from the CBD.

signature.name: Swan River
signature.detail: The river that defines Perth, with foreshore paths, ferries and views back to the skyline. Take a ferry or riverside walk at sunset; the central jetties are easy to reach on foot from Elizabeth Quay.

signature.name: Swan Bell Tower
signature.detail: A distinctive tower on the waterfront housing historic bells, with an observation deck over the river and city. Check opening hours before you go and combine it with a stroll around Elizabeth Quay.

signature.name: AQWA (The Aquarium of Western Australia)
signature.detail: A large aquarium showcasing Western Australian marine life, including a walk-through tunnel. It is a good family stop north of the city; allow a couple of hours and check feeding times on arrival.

signature.name: Art Gallery of Western Australia
signature.detail: The state art gallery in the cultural centre, with Australian and Indigenous collections and free general entry. It is a cool indoor option on hot days; it sits near the CBD and is easy to reach by train or bus.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $160 a night for two

signature.name: Independence Hall
signature.detail: The birthplace of the United States, where the Declaration of Independence and Constitution were debated and signed. It is the essential first stop for any visitor. Tickets are free but timed, so reserve online in advance and arrive at the security line early.

signature.name: Liberty Bell
signature.detail: The iconic cracked bell and symbol of American freedom sits in a free exhibit right across from Independence Hall. Entry is free and lines move quickly; go early morning to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Philadelphia Museum of Art
signature.detail: A world-class collection topped by the famous Rocky Steps and statue outside. Allow several hours for the galleries. Book tickets online and wear comfortable shoes for the climb and the large building.

signature.name: Reading Terminal Market
signature.detail: A historic indoor market packed with local food stalls, from cheesesteaks to Amish baked goods. It is the best single place to eat like a local. Come hungry on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

signature.name: Eastern State Penitentiary
signature.detail: A hauntingly preserved 19th-century prison that shaped modern incarceration, with Al Capone's cell on view. The audio tour is excellent. It is a short walk from the art museum; book ahead in autumn for the seasonal events.

signature.name: Elfreth's Alley
signature.detail: The oldest continuously inhabited residential street in the country, lined with brick colonial homes. It is a quick, free photo stop in Old City. Visit on a weekday since residents still live here.

signature.name: National Constitution Center
signature.detail: An interactive museum devoted to the US Constitution, with a dramatic theater presentation. It complements Independence Hall nearby. Check opening hours and combine it with the Old City sights.

signature.name: Philadelphia Zoo
signature.detail: America's first zoo, with a strong collection and family-friendly layout. It is a good half-day outing. Buy tickets online and go on a weekday morning for cooler, quieter visits.

food: Casual meal $12-20; cheesesteak around $10-14
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $150-250 a night
transport: SEPTA subway $2.50 a ride; walkable center

signature.name: Royal Palace of Cambodia
signature.detail: The official residence of the King and the city's most iconic sight, with the Silver Pagoda inside its walls. Go early in the morning to avoid heat and crowds; tickets are around $10 and shoulders and knees must be covered.

signature.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
signature.detail: A former school turned prison and interrogation center under the Khmer Rouge, now a sobering museum. Visit with a guide or audio tour for context; allow 1-2 hours and go early to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Killing Field
signature.detail: The Choeung Ek memorial site, where thousands were executed, is a deeply moving place with a stupa of skulls. It is about 30 minutes by tuk-tuk from the center; combine with Tuol Sleng for a full understanding of Cambodia's recent history.

signature.name: Silver Pagoda
signature.detail: Located within the Royal Palace grounds, this temple houses a floor of silver tiles and a revered emerald Buddha. Dress respectfully (no shorts or sleeveless tops) and visit in the morning when it is cooler.

signature.name: Wat Phnom
signature.detail: The city's namesake hilltop temple, a peaceful spot with good views and a lively atmosphere with monkeys and locals. It is a short walk from the riverside; go early morning or late afternoon.

signature.name: National Museum of Cambodia
signature.detail: Houses the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including sculptures from Angkor. The building itself is a beautiful example of Khmer architecture; a guide or audio tour is recommended.

signature.name: Mekong River
signature.detail: The mighty Mekong is central to Phnom Penh's identity, with lively riverfront promenades and sunset cruises. Take a boat trip at sunset for great views of the city skyline.

signature.name: Independence Monument of Cambodia
signature.detail: A striking monument in the heart of the city, especially beautiful when illuminated at night. It is a short walk from the Royal Palace and a good spot for photos.

food: About $22 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $24 a night for two
transport: About $8 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Duquesne Incline
signature.detail: A historic cable car climbing Mount Washington for one of the best skyline views in the United States, where the three rivers meet downtown. Go near sunset for the best light, and bring exact change or a card for the small fare; it is a short ride from downtown across the river.

signature.name: Point State Park
signature.detail: The green tip of downtown where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers form the Ohio, with fountains and riverfront paths. It is free and open daily; visit in the morning or late afternoon for cooler walking and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Andy Warhol Museum
signature.detail: The largest museum devoted to a single artist in North America, celebrating Pittsburgh-born Andy Warhol across seven floors. Check opening days in advance and allow at least two hours; it sits on the North Shore, walkable from downtown.

signature.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
signature.detail: A Victorian glasshouse in Schenley Park with lush seasonal displays and tropical rooms. Book timed tickets online, especially on weekends, and go early to avoid the busiest hours.

signature.name: Carnegie Museum of Natural History
signature.detail: Home to famous dinosaur skeletons and strong natural science collections in Oakland. Pair it with the adjacent art museum and check hours ahead; it is a short bus ride from downtown.

food: Casual meal $12-20; nicer dinner $30-50
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $130-200 a night
