signature.name: Aapravasi Ghat
signature.detail: This UNESCO World Heritage site is the landing point where indentured labourers arrived in Mauritius, making it the island's most important historic landmark and a must-see for understanding its people. Visit in the cooler morning hours and wear comfortable shoes, as you'll walk over stone steps and ruins.

signature.name: Le Caudan Waterfront
signature.detail: The lively harbour-side complex is Port Louis's social heart, with shops, restaurants and views over the water. Come in the late afternoon for cooler air and sunset views, and it's an easy walk from the city centre.

signature.name: Port Louis Central Market
signature.detail: The bustling central market is the best place to feel the city's everyday life, with local produce, spices and crafts. Go early in the morning for the freshest atmosphere and fewer crowds, and bring small cash for purchases.

signature.name: Citadel Fort Adelaide
signature.detail: This hilltop fort offers sweeping views over Port Louis and the harbour, making it a rewarding stop for history and photography. Visit in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat, and wear shoes suitable for walking uphill.

signature.name: Blue Penny Museum
signature.detail: Home to rare stamps and Mauritian art, this museum is a compact cultural highlight in the Caudan area. Check opening hours before you go, as it closes on some days, and allow about an hour for the visit.

signature.name: Champ de Mars Racecourse
signature.detail: One of the oldest racecourses in the southern hemisphere, it's a distinctive Port Louis experience with a colonial-era setting. Race days are the best time to visit; check the schedule in advance and dress smart-casual.

food: Casual meal $5-10; street food like dholl puri under $3
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $80-140 a night
transport: Local buses cheap; short taxi rides $5-10

signature.name: Ribeira District
signature.detail: Porto's riverside old town is a UNESCO-listed maze of narrow lanes, tiled facades and cafes spilling toward the Douro. It is the heart of the city and the best place to start a first visit. Go early in the morning to enjoy it before the crowds, and wear comfortable shoes for the cobbles and hills.

signature.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
signature.detail: This iron arch bridge is Porto's icon, linking the city with Vila Nova de Gaia across the Douro. Walk the upper deck for sweeping views, especially at sunset. The lower deck connects to Ribeira, and the upper level is reached by metro or a steep walk.

signature.name: Livraria Lello
signature.detail: One of the world's most beautiful bookshops, with a sweeping red staircase and ornate woodwork that reportedly inspired Harry Potter. Book a timed ticket online in advance, as queues are long and entry is ticketed. It is a short walk from Clerigos Tower.

signature.name: Clerigos Tower
signature.detail: This baroque tower is the city's tallest landmark and offers a panoramic view over the rooftops after a climb of around 240 steps. Climb in the morning for clearer light and shorter lines. It sits in the center, near Livraria Lello and São Bento station.

signature.name: Palácio da Bolsa
signature.detail: The former stock exchange is famous for its lavish Arabian Hall and grand interiors. Guided visits are the only way in, so check times and book ahead. It is a few minutes' walk from Ribeira and São Francisco Church.

signature.name: Porto Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's Romanesque cathedral sits on a hilltop with a terrace overlooking the old town and river. It is a calm, historic stop and a good starting point for walking down to Ribeira. Dress respectfully and go early to avoid tour groups.

food: About $71 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $162 a night for two
transport: About $23 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Old Market Square Poznań
signature.detail: Poznań's Renaissance main square is the city's living room, lined with colorful townhouses, cafés and the famous billy-goat clock nearby. Come early morning for empty cobblestones and soft light, or in the evening when the facades glow.

signature.name: Poznań Town Hall
signature.detail: This 16th-century Renaissance hall dominates the square and hides a mechanical billy-goat show that butts heads at noon daily. Arrive a few minutes before 12:00 to grab a spot in front of the clock; the interior museum is worth a short visit for its grand halls.

signature.name: Poznań Cathedral
signature.detail: Poland's oldest cathedral, on Ostrów Tumski island, holds the tombs of early Piast rulers and a golden chapel that glows at dusk. It's a 20-minute walk from the old town; check opening hours as the crypt and chapel close earlier than the nave.

signature.name: Ostrów Tumski
signature.detail: The quiet island where Poznań began, with the cathedral, old bridges and riverside paths. Cross the Warta on the Bishop Jordan Bridge for the best photo of the cathedral spires; go at sunset when the light is golden.

signature.name: Cytadela Park
signature.detail: A vast green escape on a former Prussian fort, with war memorials, sculpture trails and rose gardens. Rent a bike or walk the loop; it's a 15-minute tram ride from the center and perfect for a sunny afternoon.

signature.name: Poznań International Fair grounds
signature.detail: A striking complex of early-20th-century pavilions that still hosts trade fairs and events. Even when closed, the architecture is worth a stroll; check the fair calendar for open days or guided walks.

food: About $19 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $36 a night for two
transport: About $4 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Shaniwar Wada
signature.detail: The fortified palace of the Peshwas is Pune's defining monument, famous for its massive gates and the stories tied to its ruins. Go early morning to avoid the heat and crowds, and note the entry ticket is small but paid.

signature.name: Aga Khan Palace
signature.detail: A grand palace with serene gardens, best known as the place where Mahatma Gandhi was interned. It is a peaceful, must-see stop; visit in the cooler morning hours and allow an hour or two.

signature.name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
signature.detail: One of Pune's most beloved and visited temples, dedicated to Lord Ganesha and especially vibrant during festivals. Dress modestly, remove shoes, and expect queues; early morning is calmest.

signature.name: Sinhagad Fort
signature.detail: A hill fort with sweeping views and a strong place in Maratha history, popular for a half-day trip from the city. Go early to beat the heat and traffic, and wear shoes with grip for the uneven paths.

signature.name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
signature.detail: A rock-cut cave temple carved from basalt, right in the middle of the city and a quiet contrast to the busy streets. It is quick to see; combine it with nearby central sights and visit in daylight hours.

food: About $21 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $38 a night for two
transport: About $8 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Tsingtao Brewery Museum
signature.detail: The birthplace of China's most famous beer, where you can tour historic brewing halls and sample fresh Tsingtao. Go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and bring ID for the tasting.

signature.name: Zhanqiao Pier
signature.detail: Qingdao's iconic 440-meter pier stretching into the sea, ending at a pavilion with great views of the coastline. Visit at sunset for the best photos, and walk there from the old town.

signature.name: St. Michael's Cathedral
signature.detail: A striking Gothic-style church in the heart of the old town, popular for its architecture and hilltop setting. Dress respectfully, and note that a small entry fee applies.

signature.name: May Fourth Square
signature.detail: A modern waterfront plaza famous for its red 'May Wind' sculpture and sea views. It's free and especially lively in the evening when locals gather.

signature.name: Badaguan Scenic Area
signature.detail: A leafy neighborhood of historic villas from various European styles, best explored on foot. Come in spring or autumn for pleasant weather and fewer tourists.

signature.name: No. 1 Bathing Beach
signature.detail: Qingdao's most popular sandy beach, close to the old town and ideal for a summer swim. Bring your own towel and go early to rent an umbrella.

signature.name: Laoshan Mountain
signature.detail: A sacred Taoist mountain with hiking trails, temples, and coastal views. Allow a full day, wear comfortable shoes, and take the bus or cable car up.

signature.name: Qingdao Olympic Sailing Center
signature.detail: The 2008 Olympic sailing venue, now a marina with waterfront promenades and cafes. Visit in the late afternoon for a stroll and sea breeze.

food: About $37 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $56 a night for two
transport: About $13 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Historic Centre of Quito
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed colonial old town packed with churches, plazas and balconied streets, and the first thing any visitor should explore. Go early in the morning for quieter streets and better light; it is walkable from most central hotels and taxis are cheap.

signature.name: Middle of the World City
signature.detail: The monument marking the equator, where you can stand with a foot in each hemisphere, is Quito's most famous photo stop. It is north of the city, so allow half a day and take a taxi or tour bus; go on a clear morning for views.

signature.name: Church of the Society of Jesus
signature.detail: This Jesuit church is famous for its gold-leaf interior and is one of the most ornate sights in the old town. Dress respectfully and note that a small entry fee applies; visit early or late to avoid tour groups.

signature.name: Virgin of El Panecillo
signature.detail: A huge winged statue on a hill with panoramic views over Quito and the surrounding volcanoes. Go on a clear day and take a taxi up rather than walking, especially after dark.

signature.name: Basilica of the National Vow
signature.detail: A neo-Gothic basilica with towers you can climb for rooftop views over the old town. Wear comfortable shoes for the stairs and ladders; a small fee is charged to go up.

food: Casual meal $5-10; mid-range dinner $12-20
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $50-90 a night
transport: Metro $0.35 a ride; taxis short trips $2-4

signature.name: Riga Old Town
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed maze of cobbled lanes, medieval churches and merchant houses that is the heart of any first visit. Go early in the morning to enjoy the squares before the crowds arrive.

signature.name: House of the Blackheads
signature.detail: This ornate 14th-century guild hall, rebuilt after WWII, is one of Riga's most photographed buildings. Buy a ticket to see the lavish interior and climb to the small museum upstairs.

signature.name: Freedom Monument
signature.detail: A towering symbol of Latvian independence guarded by soldiers, located between Old Town and the Art Nouveau District. Visit at dusk when it is softly lit, and watch the changing of the guard on the hour.

signature.name: Art Nouveau District
signature.detail: Several streets are lined with spectacular early-20th-century facades, many designed by Mikhail Eisenstein. Take a self-guided walk along Alberta iela; the Riga Art Nouveau Museum is a worthwhile stop.

signature.name: Riga Central Market
signature.detail: Housed in converted Zeppelin hangars, this is one of Europe's largest markets and a great place to taste local produce. Go hungry and try grey peas with bacon at one of the food stalls.

signature.name: Riga Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's largest medieval church, famous for its massive organ and cloister. Climb the tower for a panoramic view of Old Town; entry to the tower is ticketed separately.

signature.name: St. Peter's Church
signature.detail: Its slender spire dominates the skyline and the viewing platform offers the best panorama of Riga. Take the lift up (small fee) on a clear day for photos.

signature.name: Latvian National Opera
signature.detail: A grand 19th-century theatre with affordable tickets and excellent productions. Check the schedule for opera or ballet; the building itself is worth a look even without a show.

signature.name: Daugava River
signature.detail: The wide river divides Old Town from the newer districts and offers pleasant promenades. Walk along the embankment at sunset for views of the skyline and bridges.

signature.name: Jūrmala Resort
signature.detail: A short train ride from Riga, this seaside town has a long sandy beach and wooden villas. It is a perfect half-day escape in summer; trains run frequently from Riga Central Station.

food: About $64 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $116 a night for two
transport: About $11 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Christ the Redeemer
signature.detail: Rio's defining icon, a colossal Art Deco statue atop Corcovado with sweeping views over the city, bay and mountains. Go early in the morning for clearer skies and fewer crowds, and book official tickets online in advance; the usual access is by the Corcovado train or van from Cosme Velho.

signature.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
signature.detail: The second postcard sight, reached by a two-stage cable car with panoramic views of Guanabara Bay and the beaches. Late afternoon is best so you catch sunset, and buying tickets online saves queueing time.

signature.name: Copacabana Beach
signature.detail: The world-famous crescent of sand and wave-patterned promenade, essential for the classic Rio beach experience. Mornings are calmer for swimming and walking; keep valuables minimal and watch your belongings on busy days.

signature.name: Ipanema Beach
signature.detail: Rio's stylish beach, backed by the Dois Irmãos peaks and known for its lively postos (lifeguard stations) that each draw a different crowd. Weekday mornings are quieter; bring cash for beach vendors and avoid bringing valuables.

signature.name: Maracanã
signature.detail: One of the world's legendary football stadiums and a pilgrimage for fans. Check the schedule for a match or take a stadium tour; match days are electric but book tickets well ahead.

signature.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian
signature.detail: A striking modern cathedral shaped like a Mayan pyramid, with soaring stained glass inside. It is in central Rio, easy to combine with Lapa and the Lapa Arches; entry is free and it is open daily.

signature.name: Escadaria Selarón
signature.detail: The colorful tiled staircase in Lapa, a beloved photo spot and symbol of the city's bohemian spirit. Visit early to avoid crowds, and combine it with a walk through Lapa's nightlife streets.

food: About $34 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $130 a night for two
transport: About $8 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Kingdom Centre
signature.detail: Riyadh's most recognizable skyscraper, with a sky bridge offering sweeping views over the city. Go near sunset for the best light; tickets for the sky bridge are sold on site, and modest dress is expected.

signature.name: Diriyah
signature.detail: The historic birthplace of the Saudi state, with mud-brick ruins and a growing cultural district. Visit in the cooler evening hours; the At-Turaif District within Diriyah is a UNESCO site and requires a ticket.

signature.name: Masmak Fortress
signature.detail: A 19th-century castle in the heart of old Riyadh, central to Saudi history. It is free to enter and best visited in the morning; modest dress is advised.

food: Casual meal $5-10; mid-range dinner $15-25
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $80-140 a night
transport: Taxis and ride-hailing $3-8 a trip; metro $1-2

signature.name: Erasmus Bridge
signature.detail: Rotterdam's modern icon, a striking white cable-stayed bridge over the Maas that has become the symbol of the rebuilt city. Walk or cycle across for free views of the skyline, and come at sunset or after dark when it is lit up.

signature.name: Cube Houses
signature.detail: A cluster of tilted, cube-shaped homes balanced on pillars, one of the city's most photographed modern sights. You can pay a small fee to visit the Show Cube museum inside; it is a short walk from Blaak station.

signature.name: Markthal
signature.detail: A huge arched market hall with a colourful ceiling mural, packed with food stalls, bars and shops. It is busiest at lunchtime, so go early morning or late afternoon for a calmer browse; it sits right beside the Cube Houses.

signature.name: Euromast
signature.detail: A tall observation tower offering the best panoramic view over Rotterdam and its port. Book tickets online to skip queues and go on a clear day; you can also take the rotating elevator up for an extra charge.

food: About $99 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $184 a night for two
transport: About $29 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: San Diego Zoo
signature.detail: One of the world's most celebrated zoos, home to pandas, elephants and a huge collection set in Balboa Park's canyons. Buy tickets online in advance for a discount, and arrive at opening to beat the crowds and heat.

signature.name: Balboa Park
signature.detail: A sprawling cultural park with museums, gardens and Spanish colonial architecture, and the zoo sits within it. Go on a weekday morning, wear comfortable shoes, and use the free tram to get around.

signature.name: USS Midway Museum
signature.detail: Tour a decommissioned aircraft carrier docked downtown, with planes on deck and crew quarters below. Book online, allow at least three hours, and go early to avoid the midday sun on the flight deck.

signature.name: La Jolla Cove
signature.detail: A scenic cove with sea lions, tide pools and clear water for snorkeling and kayaking. Visit early morning for fewer crowds and better wildlife viewing, and keep a respectful distance from the sea lions.

signature.name: Coronado Beach
signature.detail: A wide, golden-sand beach with the historic Hotel del Coronado as its backdrop. Take the ferry or drive over the bridge, and go in the late afternoon for softer light and fewer people.

signature.name: Cabrillo National Monument
signature.detail: A clifftop monument with sweeping views over the harbor, the city and the Pacific, plus a historic lighthouse. Drive or take a rideshare to Point Loma, and come on a clear day for the best views.

signature.name: Old Town San Diego
signature.detail: The historic birthplace of the city, with adobe buildings, museums and Mexican restaurants. It is easy to reach by trolley; go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

signature.name: San Diego Harbor Cruise
signature.detail: A boat tour of the harbor showing the skyline, naval ships and the Coronado Bridge from the water. Book a late-afternoon departure for cooler air and good light, and bring a light jacket for the breeze.

food: Casual meal $15-25; sit-down dinner $30-50
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $180-280 a night
transport: Trolley or bus $2.50 a ride; rideshares moderate

signature.name: Golden Gate Bridge
signature.detail: The world's most photographed bridge, an engineering marvel and symbol of San Francisco. Walk or bike across for free; go early morning to avoid fog and crowds, or late afternoon for golden light.

signature.name: Alcatraz
signature.detail: The infamous former federal prison on an island in the bay, now a national park with a gripping audio tour. Book tickets well in advance (often weeks ahead) and take the ferry from Pier 33; dress in layers as it's windy and cool.

signature.name: Fisherman's Wharf
signature.detail: A lively waterfront hub with sea lions at Pier 39, clam chowder in sourdough bowls, and views of Alcatraz. Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds; it's easily reached by cable car or F-line streetcar.

signature.name: Cable Cars
signature.detail: The world's last manually operated cable car system, a moving National Historic Landmark. Ride the Powell-Hyde line from Union Square to Fisherman's Wharf; board at the turnaround for a seat and hold on tight on the hills.

signature.name: Painted Ladies
signature.detail: The iconic row of Victorian houses on Alamo Square, best known from the 'Full House' opening credits. Combine with a picnic in Alamo Square Park; go on a clear day for skyline views behind the houses.

signature.name: Palace of Fine Arts
signature.detail: A stunning Beaux-Arts rotunda and lagoon built for the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition. It's free to visit; go at sunset for romantic photos, and walk over from Crissy Field or the Marina.

signature.name: Golden Gate Park
signature.detail: A vast urban park larger than Central Park, home to gardens, museums, and bison. Rent a bike or take a picnic; don't miss the Japanese Tea Garden and the de Young Museum.

signature.name: Twin Peaks
signature.detail: Two hills offering the best panoramic views of the city and bay. Drive or take a rideshare up; go at sunset or night for sparkling city lights, but bring a jacket as it's windy and cold.

signature.name: Lombard Street
signature.detail: The famous 'crookedest street' with eight hairpin turns on a steep block. Walk down the stairs on either side for free; driving it is fun but expect queues, so go early morning.

signature.name: Coit Tower
signature.detail: An Art Deco tower on Telegraph Hill with 360-degree views and WPA-era murals inside. Take the elevator to the top for a small fee; walk up the Filbert Steps for a scenic approach.

food: Casual meal $15-25; mid-range dinner $30-50 per person
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $200-350 a night; budget options from $120

signature.name: Winchester Mystery House
signature.detail: A sprawling Victorian mansion famous for its maze-like layout, staircases to nowhere and doors that open onto walls. It is San Jose's most distinctive attraction and a must for first-time visitors. Book tickets online in advance and go early in the day to avoid the biggest crowds.

signature.name: Tech Interactive
signature.detail: An interactive science and technology museum in downtown San Jose with hands-on exhibits that suit both kids and adults. It is a good rainy-day or family stop. Check opening days before you go, as hours vary by season.

signature.name: Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum
signature.detail: Houses one of the larger collections of Egyptian artifacts on the US West Coast, set in a distinctive Egyptian-style building. It is a quieter, focused museum that rewards a couple of hours. Allow extra time to walk the surrounding park.

signature.name: San Jose Municipal Rose Garden
signature.detail: A free, well-kept rose garden that is especially pretty in spring and early summer when the blooms peak. It is an easy, relaxing stop. Visit in the morning for softer light and fewer people.

signature.name: Plaza de Cesar Chavez
signature.detail: The central downtown square, close to museums and the Tech Interactive, and a natural starting point for a walking day. It often hosts events. Combine it with nearby downtown sights rather than making a special trip.

signature.name: San Pedro Square Market
signature.detail: A lively downtown market hall with many food stalls and a sociable atmosphere, good for a casual meal. It is a practical lunch or dinner stop near the other downtown sights. Go slightly off peak hours to find seating.

signature.name: History Park
signature.detail: An outdoor history park with historic buildings and exhibits that give a sense of the region's past. It is a pleasant, low-key stop, especially for families. Check the schedule, as some buildings open only at certain times.

signature.name: San Jose Museum of Art
signature.detail: A downtown art museum with a focus on modern and contemporary work. It pairs well with the Tech Interactive and the plaza for a compact downtown day. Confirm current exhibitions and hours before visiting.

stay: Good 3-4* hotel $150-250 a night
transport: Light rail around $2.50 a ride; rideshares common

signature.name: National Theatre of Costa Rica
signature.detail: The country's grandest cultural building, an ornate 1897 theater with a gilded interior and marble lobby that is a symbol of San José's coffee-era wealth. It anchors the Plaza de la Cultura, so you can combine it with the museums nearby. Go on a weekday morning for guided tours and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Pre-Columbian Gold Museum
signature.detail: Houses a stunning collection of gold artifacts from Costa Rica's indigenous cultures, displayed in underground galleries beneath the Plaza de la Cultura. It is compact and easy to pair with the National Theatre. Buy tickets at the entrance and allow about an hour.

signature.name: National Museum of Costa Rica
signature.detail: Set in a former fortress with a butterfly garden and a bullet-marked wall, it tells the country's history from pre-Columbian times to the 1948 civil war. It is a short walk from the city center. Visit in the morning to avoid afternoon rain.

signature.name: Jade Museum
signature.detail: A well-organized museum with the largest collection of American jade, plus other pre-Columbian artifacts, in a modern building. It is a good rainy-day stop and close to the National Museum. Check opening hours, as it closes some days.

signature.name: Metallic Building
signature.detail: A striking prefabricated iron building from the late 19th century, shipped from Europe and now a cultural landmark in the city center. It is best seen from the outside and is a quick photo stop. Combine it with a walk through the nearby Mercado Central.

stay: Mid-range hotel about $108 a night for two

signature.name: San Salvador Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's central church and the burial site of Archbishop Óscar Romero, it anchors the historic heart around Plaza Barrios. Visit in the morning on a weekday for quieter access, and dress modestly since it is an active place of worship.

signature.name: Monument to the Divine Savior of the World
signature.detail: This tall statue of Christ is the city's best-known symbol and a natural photo stop. Come in the late afternoon for softer light, and note it sits along a busy boulevard so arrange a taxi or rideshare rather than walking far.

signature.name: Iglesia El Rosario
signature.detail: A striking modern church famous for its curved concrete shell and rainbow-colored stained glass. Go on a sunny morning when the light through the glass is at its best, and keep quiet as services may be underway.

signature.name: Joya de Ceren
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed archaeological site often called the Pompeii of the Americas, where a buried farming village is preserved. It lies outside the city, so plan a half-day trip with transport arranged in advance and bring sun protection.

signature.name: National Theater of San Salvador
signature.detail: A restored historic theater that is a highlight of the downtown architecture. Check the schedule for performances or guided visits, and go during daylight hours when the surrounding streets are busiest.

signature.name: Plaza Libertad
signature.detail: A central historical square surrounded by landmarks and good for a short orientation walk. Stop by in the morning, and keep valuables close in this busy downtown area.

signature.name: Parque Cuscatlán
signature.detail: The city's main urban park, with green space and memorials, good for a relaxed break. Visit on weekends when locals gather, and avoid the park after dark.

stay: Good 3-4* hotel $70-120 a night

signature.name: Cerro San Cristóbal
signature.detail: Santiago's green hill rises above the city and gives the classic panorama of the Andes and the urban sprawl. Ride the Teleférico or the funicular up and go early in the morning for clearer skies and shorter queues.

signature.name: La Moneda Palace
signature.detail: Chile's presidential palace is the political heart of the country and a handsome neoclassical landmark on the civic square. Free guided visits need booking ahead; otherwise admire it from the Plaza de la Constitución and catch the changing of the guard.

signature.name: Plaza de Armas of Santiago
signature.detail: The historic core of the city, ringed by the cathedral and colonial-era buildings, is the natural starting point for a walk. Come in the morning to see it before the crowds, and watch your belongings in the busy square.

signature.name: Sky Costanera
signature.detail: The observation deck atop South America's tallest building offers a 360-degree view over Santiago and the mountains beyond. Go near sunset for the best light, and buy tickets online to skip the line.

signature.name: Santa Lucia Hill
signature.detail: This small rocky hill in the center has terraces, fountains and a neo-classical lookout with fine city views. It is an easy, free stop on a walking day; climb in the morning before the heat.

signature.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago
signature.detail: The city's main cathedral faces the Plaza de Armas and is worth a look for its colonial facade and richly decorated interior. Entry is free; dress modestly and visit outside mass times.

signature.name: Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino
signature.detail: One of Latin America's best collections of pre-Columbian art, housed in the old royal customs building. Allow a couple of hours; it is a short walk from the Plaza de Armas and closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Sanctuary of the Immaculate Conception
signature.detail: The white statue of the Virgin crowns Cerro San Cristóbal and is a pilgrimage site with sweeping views. Combine it with the cable car or funicular ride up the hill and go on a clear day.

signature.name: Ciudad Colonial
signature.detail: The walled old town is the heart of the first European city in the Americas, packed with colonial streets, plazas and churches. Wander it on foot early in the morning before the heat and crowds build, and wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones.

signature.name: Alcazar de Colon
signature.detail: This palace built for Diego Columbus is the city's most striking colonial residence and a must for understanding its Spanish heritage. Check opening hours before you go, as they can vary, and go early to avoid tour groups.

signature.name: Ozama Fortress
signature.detail: The oldest military fortress in the Americas guards the river mouth and offers some of the best views over the old town. Bring water and sun protection, as the grounds are largely open to the sun.

signature.name: Catedral Primada de América
signature.detail: The first cathedral in the Americas anchors the old town and is a landmark of colonial architecture. Dress modestly, as it is an active church, and visit outside mass times.

signature.name: Ibirapuera Park
signature.detail: São Paulo's most famous park and a must-see for its green space, museums and lakes. Go early on a weekday to avoid crowds; it's free and easily reached by metro and bus.

signature.name: São Paulo Museum of Art
signature.detail: Home to one of Latin America's finest art collections and an iconic modernist building on Paulista Avenue. Closed on Mondays; check ticket prices online and arrive early on weekends.

signature.name: Paulista Avenue
signature.detail: The city's main artery, packed with museums, shops and cultural institutions. Visit on a Sunday when the avenue is closed to cars and becomes a lively open street.

signature.name: Mercado Municipal de Sao Paulo

signature.name: Neve Tzedek
signature.detail: One of the city's oldest neighborhoods, now a charming maze of restored houses, galleries and quiet lanes. Wander on a weekday morning when it is calm, and dress casually for walking.

signature.name: Carmel Market
signature.detail: The bustling open-air market is the best place to taste local food and feel the city's everyday energy. Come before noon on Friday for the fullest stalls, and bring cash for snacks.

signature.name: Bauhaus/White City architecture
signature.detail: Tel Aviv holds one of the world's great collections of Bauhaus and International Style buildings, a UNESCO-listed draw. A self-guided walk is free; start in the morning to avoid the midday sun.

signature.name: Rothschild Boulevard
signature.detail: This leafy boulevard mixes historic buildings, cafes and the story of the city's founding. It is free and pleasant to stroll in the late afternoon or evening.

signature.name: HaYarkon Park
signature.detail: The city's largest green space offers lawns, paths and river-side walks for a break from the streets. Early morning or late afternoon is coolest; entry is free.

signature.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
signature.detail: A major museum with a strong modern and Israeli collection, worth a half day for art lovers. Check opening hours and ticket prices ahead, as some days are shorter.

signature.name: Tianjin Eye
signature.detail: The giant Ferris wheel straddling the Haihe River is Tianjin's most recognizable sight and a classic photo stop. Ride it in the late afternoon or after dark for the best views of the river and skyline. Tickets are sold on site; expect queues on weekends.

signature.name: Five Great Avenues
signature.detail: This old-town district is famous for its streets of European-style villas and quiet tree-lined lanes. It is best explored on foot or by bike in the morning when it is quieter. No ticket is needed to wander the streets.

signature.name: Ancient Culture Street
signature.detail: A traditional-style pedestrian street with old architecture, local crafts and snacks, ideal for a first taste of Tianjin's folk culture. Go on a weekday to avoid the heaviest crowds, and bring cash for small vendors.

signature.name: Italian Style Town
signature.detail: A compact quarter of Italianate buildings and squares that makes an easy, photogenic stroll near the river. Combine it with the Haihe River waterfront for a pleasant half-day walk.

signature.name: Haihe River waterfront
signature.detail: The river promenade is the city's scenic spine and especially lovely at dusk when the bridges and buildings light up. A riverside walk or short boat ride is a relaxed way to see the city.

signature.name: Porcelain House
signature.detail: A striking artwork of a building covered in porcelain and antiques, unlike anything else in the city. Check opening hours before going, as visiting times can be limited.

signature.name: Tianjin Binhai Library
signature.detail: The futuristic library with its famous spherical atrium is a must for architecture and photo fans. Entry is generally free but may require advance booking; go early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Tianjin Museum
signature.detail: The city's main museum holds strong collections of Chinese art and local history, and is a good rainy-day or hot-afternoon stop. It is usually free with ID; closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Skanderbeg Square
signature.detail: Tirana's vast central plaza is the heart of the city and the natural starting point for any visit, ringed by the mosque, clock tower and national museum. Come early morning or after sunset when the lights come on and the square is at its most atmospheric; it is free and open at all hours.

signature.name: Enver Hoxha Pyramid
signature.detail: This striking concrete pyramid, built as a monument to the communist dictator, is Tirana's most talked-about piece of brutalist heritage and a favorite spot for photos and views. It sits a short walk from Skanderbeg Square; go in the late afternoon for softer light and fewer people.

signature.name: Bunk'Art 1 Museum
signature.detail: A sprawling Cold War bunker turned museum that gives a gripping look at Albania's communist past through its tunnels and rooms. It is a few kilometers from the center, so take a taxi or local bus; allow at least an hour and check opening hours before you go.

signature.name: National Historical Museum
signature.detail: The country's main museum covers Albanian history from antiquity through the communist era, with the famous mosaic on its facade. It faces Skanderbeg Square, making it easy to combine with the square and mosque; a couple of hours is enough for the highlights.

signature.name: Ethem Bey Mosque
signature.detail: A graceful 18th-century mosque right on Skanderbeg Square, known for its painted interior and peaceful courtyard. It is an active place of worship, so dress modestly and avoid visiting during prayer times; entry is free.

signature.name: Tirana Clock Tower
signature.detail: The slender Ottoman-era clock tower next to the mosque is one of the city's best-loved symbols and offers a quick climb for a view over the square. It is steps from Skanderbeg Square; go on a clear day and watch your footing on the narrow stairs.

signature.name: Blloku district
signature.detail: Once the sealed-off neighborhood for communist elites, Blloku is now Tirana's liveliest area for cafes, bars and evening strolls. It is a short walk south of the center; come in the evening when the streets fill up.

signature.name: Resurrection of Christ Orthodox Cathedral
signature.detail: A modern Orthodox cathedral with a distinctive domed and arched design, worth a look for its frescoed interior. It is near the center and free to enter; dress respectfully and keep quiet during services.

signature.name: CN Tower
signature.detail: Toronto's defining icon and one of the tallest freestanding structures in the world, with sweeping views over the city and Lake Ontario. Book tickets online in advance to skip lines, and go near sunset for the best light.

signature.name: Royal Ontario Museum
signature.detail: Canada's largest museum, mixing natural history, world cultures and dinosaurs in a striking crystal-clad building. Allow at least half a day and check for discounted evening hours.

signature.name: Distillery District
signature.detail: A pedestrian-only historic district of Victorian industrial buildings now filled with galleries, shops and cafes. It is a pleasant stroll any time; visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
signature.detail: A large aquarium beside the CN Tower with walk-through tunnels and sharks overhead, great for families. Buy timed tickets online and go early on weekends.

signature.name: St. Lawrence Market
signature.detail: A beloved historic market with food stalls, local produce and the famous peameal bacon sandwich. Come hungry on a Saturday morning when it is liveliest.

signature.name: Casa Loma
signature.detail: A grand early-20th-century castle with towers, gardens and secret passages to explore. Take the audio guide and allow a couple of hours.

signature.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
signature.detail: A major art museum with a celebrated Frank Gehry-designed facade and a strong Canadian and international collection. Check for free or reduced admission nights.

signature.name: Toronto Islands
signature.detail: Car-free islands just offshore with beaches, bike paths and skyline views back at the city. Take the ferry from the harbour and bring a picnic.

signature.name: Medina of Tunis
signature.detail: The UNESCO-listed old town is the heart of the city, a dense maze of souks, mosques and historic houses that rewards wandering. Go in the morning when the markets are lively but less crowded, and dress modestly for mosque visits. It sits right by the central station, so you can walk in from Bab El Bhar.

signature.name: Sidi Bou Said
signature.detail: The blue-and-white clifftop village is Tunis's most photographed spot, with sea views and charming lanes. Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and take the TGM light rail from the city center. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobbled slopes.

signature.name: Bardo National Museum
signature.detail: Home to one of the world's finest collections of Roman mosaics, this is a must for anyone interested in Tunisia's layered history. Allow at least two hours and check opening days before you go, as hours can vary. It is a short taxi or metro ride from the center.

signature.name: Archaeological Site of Carthage
signature.detail: The sprawling ruins of ancient Carthage, including baths and villas, are a highlight for history lovers. The site is spread out, so plan to take a taxi between the main areas. Bring water and sun protection, as shade is limited.

signature.name: Zitouna Mosque
signature.detail: The city's principal mosque sits at the center of the Medina and anchors its spiritual life. Non-Muslims may not enter the prayer hall, but the courtyard and surroundings are worth seeing. Visit outside prayer times and dress conservatively.

signature.name: Mole Antonelliana
signature.detail: Turin's unmistakable symbol, a soaring 19th-century tower that houses the National Museum of Cinema. Ride the glass lift to the top for panoramic city views; book tickets online to skip the queue, and go early or late for softer light.

signature.name: Egyptian Museum, Turin
signature.detail: One of the world's great Egyptology collections, second only to Cairo, with mummies, statues and papyri. Allow at least two hours; buy timed tickets in advance and avoid Monday closures.

signature.name: Royal Palace of Turin
signature.detail: The opulent former residence of the House of Savoy, a UNESCO site with lavish halls and armories. Visit in the morning when it's quieter, and note that some areas require a guided tour.

signature.name: La Venaria Reale
signature.detail: A vast baroque palace and garden complex on the city's edge, often called Italy's Versailles. Take the train or bus from Turin, and set aside a half-day to explore the gardens and exhibitions.

signature.name: Basilica of Superga
signature.detail: A hilltop basilica with sweeping views over Turin and the Alps, reached by a historic rack railway or bus. Dress respectfully, and check opening hours as the church closes at midday.

signature.name: Piazza Castello
signature.detail: The elegant heart of baroque Turin, lined with palaces and arcades. It's a natural starting point for a walking tour; come in the late afternoon for a coffee under the porticoes.

signature.name: City of Arts and Sciences
signature.detail: Valencia's futuristic complex of white curves and glass is the city's modern icon and a must-see for any first-time visitor. Book tickets online for the aquarium and science museum to skip queues, and go early morning or at dusk for cooler weather and better photos.

signature.name: Valencia Cathedral
signature.detail: This cathedral holds the claimed Holy Grail and mixes Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque styles in one building. Climb the tower for city views, and dress modestly since it is an active place of worship.

signature.name: Central Market of Valencia
signature.detail: One of Europe's largest and most beautiful covered markets, a feast of fresh produce and local snacks under a stained-glass dome. Arrive before noon for the fullest stalls, and note it closes on Sundays.

signature.name: Turia Gardens (Jardín del Turia)
signature.detail: A green ribbon running through the city in a former riverbed, perfect for walking or cycling between the old town and the City of Arts and Sciences. Go in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat.

signature.name: La Lonja de la Seda
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed Gothic silk exchange with a stunning spiral-columned hall, a short walk from the Central Market. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter rooms and combine it with the market next door.

signature.name: Torres de Serranos
signature.detail: These medieval gate towers once guarded the city and now offer a short climb with fine views over the old town. Go late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Stanley Park
signature.detail: Vancouver's defining green space, a huge waterfront park with a famous seawall, beaches and old-growth forest. It is the first place most visitors head for. Tip: walk or cycle the seawall early in the morning to avoid crowds, and rent a bike near the entrance.

signature.name: Granville Island
signature.detail: A lively urban hub with a public market, food stalls, galleries and waterfront views. It is a must-see for the atmosphere and local food. Tip: take the small False Creek ferry across for a scenic and cheap arrival.

signature.name: Canada Place
signature.detail: The sail-roofed pier on the downtown waterfront, one of the city's most recognizable sights. It offers views over the harbour and mountains. Tip: go on a clear day for the best photos and combine it with a walk along the waterfront.

signature.name: Gastown Steam Clock
signature.detail: A quirky steam-powered clock in the historic Gastown district, a classic photo stop. The surrounding cobbled streets are good for a wander. Tip: it whistles on the quarter hour, so time your visit to hear it.

signature.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
signature.detail: A dramatic suspension bridge over a forested canyon, a top attraction just outside downtown. It is popular for the treetop walkways and cliff walk. Tip: book tickets online and arrive early, as it gets busy midday.

signature.name: Grouse Mountain
signature.detail: A mountain with a gondola ride and sweeping views over the city and coast. It is a signature Vancouver experience. Tip: check the weather before going, since views disappear in cloud, and dress warmly at the top.

signature.name: Vancouver Aquarium
signature.detail: A well-known aquarium inside Stanley Park with marine exhibits and family-friendly displays. It pairs naturally with a park visit. Tip: buy tickets ahead and go on a weekday morning for fewer crowds.

signature.name: Lions Gate Bridge
signature.detail: An iconic green suspension bridge linking downtown to the North Shore, with great views. It is a landmark worth seeing even briefly. Tip: walk or cycle across for the best experience, as parking nearby is limited.

signature.name: Schönbrunn Palace
signature.detail: The Habsburgs' summer residence is Vienna's most visited sight, with grand state rooms and vast gardens. Book a timed ticket online to skip the queue, and go early morning to beat the crowds.

signature.name: Hofburg Palace
signature.detail: The sprawling imperial palace in the city center housed the Habsburg court for centuries. Visit the imperial apartments and the Sisi Museum, and note the complex is a short walk from the U3 Herrengasse stop.

signature.name: St Stephen's Cathedral
signature.detail: The Gothic cathedral with its patterned roof is the heart of the old town. Climb the south tower for views or take the lift up the north tower; entry to the nave is free but towers are ticketed.

signature.name: Belvedere Palace
signature.detail: The baroque palace houses Austrian art including Klimt's The Kiss. Buy tickets online and allow time for the gardens between the Upper and Lower palaces.

signature.name: Vienna State Opera
signature.detail: One of the world's great opera houses, central to Vienna's musical identity. Standing-room tickets are sold cheaply on the day, and guided tours run when there is no rehearsal.

signature.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
signature.detail: A world-class art museum in a magnificent building on the Ringstrasse. Go on a weekday morning for quieter galleries, and don't miss the Kunstkammer collection.

signature.name: MuseumsQuartier
signature.detail: A lively cultural quarter with major museums, courtyards and outdoor seating. It's a good base for an afternoon, with the Leopold Museum and mumok on site.

signature.name: Naschmarkt
signature.detail: Vienna's best-known market, with produce stalls, spices and casual eateries. Come on a weekday morning; Saturdays are busy and the flea market runs on Saturdays.

signature.name: Warsaw Old Town
signature.detail: The reconstructed heart of the city, rebuilt brick by brick after WWII and now a UNESCO site. It is the essential first stop for any visitor. Go early in the morning to enjoy the squares before the crowds arrive.

signature.name: Palace of Culture and Science
signature.detail: A towering Soviet-era landmark that dominates the skyline and houses museums, theatres and a viewing terrace. Head up to the terrace for panoramic views, ideally around sunset. Buy tickets on arrival.

signature.name: Royal Castle, Warsaw
signature.detail: The former residence of Polish kings on Castle Square, richly restored with grand interiors. It anchors the Old Town and is a must for history lovers. Book tickets ahead in peak season to skip the queue.

signature.name: Łazienki Palace
signature.detail: An elegant palace on an island in the middle of a beautiful park, surrounded by gardens and peacocks. It is a peaceful escape from the busy centre. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter paths.

signature.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
signature.detail: A striking modern museum telling a thousand years of Jewish history in Poland. It is one of the city's most acclaimed cultural sights. Allow at least half a day and check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
signature.detail: A powerful, immersive museum devoted to the 1944 uprising, with moving exhibits and artefacts. It is essential for understanding the city's modern identity. Book timed tickets in advance.

signature.name: Wilanów Palace
signature.detail: A baroque royal palace with formal gardens on the city's southern edge. It makes a rewarding half-day trip away from the centre. Take a bus or taxi and go early to beat the crowds.

signature.name: Lincoln Memorial
signature.detail: The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic must-see with its massive statue and famous steps overlooking the Reflecting Pool. Visit early morning to avoid crowds and see the monument in soft light; it's free and open 24 hours.

signature.name: National Mall
signature.detail: The National Mall is the heart of the capital, a grand park lined with monuments and museums. Walk it at sunrise or rent a bike to cover more ground; most monuments are free and accessible.

signature.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
signature.detail: Home to the Hope Diamond and dinosaur skeletons, this museum is a favorite for all ages. Admission is free; arrive at opening to beat the crowds, especially on weekends.

signature.name: The White House
signature.detail: The White House is the president's residence and a symbol of American democracy. Public tours require advance requests through your member of Congress; view it from Lafayette Square if tickets aren't available.

signature.name: United States Capitol
signature.detail: The Capitol is where Congress meets and offers free tours of the rotunda and chambers. Book tours online in advance; the visitor center is accessible via Union Station Metro.

signature.name: National Gallery of Art
signature.detail: This world-class museum houses masterpieces from da Vinci to Van Gogh, including 'Luncheon of the Boating Party'. Free entry; start with the West Building for classic works and take a break in the sculpture garden.

signature.name: Washington Monument
signature.detail: The Washington Monument offers the best panoramic views of the city from its observation deck. Free timed tickets are required; reserve online or arrive early for same-day tickets.

signature.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
signature.detail: See the Wright Flyer and Apollo 11 command module in this tribute to flight. Free admission; timed-entry passes are required, so book online before your visit.

signature.name: Te Papa Tongarewa
signature.detail: New Zealand's national museum and the city's headline attraction, with strong Maori and Pacific collections plus natural history and art. Entry to the main exhibitions is free, so go early in the day to beat the school groups, and allow at least half a day.

signature.name: Wellington Botanic Garden
signature.detail: A large hillside garden reached by the historic cable car from Lambton Quay, with views over the city and harbour. It is free to enter; ride up and walk back down through the gardens for the best value.

signature.name: Mount Victoria Lookout
signature.detail: The classic viewpoint over the city and harbour, a short drive or a steady walk up from the central city. Go on a clear morning for the sharpest views, and bring a windproof layer as it is exposed.

signature.name: Zealandia
signature.detail: A predator-fenced valley sanctuary where native birds such as tui and kaka are easy to see close to the city. Book a daytime entry ticket online and wear walking shoes; the trails take a few hours.

signature.name: Wellington Waterfront
signature.detail: A flat, lively promenade linking the harbour, Te Papa and the city's cafes, good for an easy stroll any time of day. Walk it in the late afternoon when the light is best and the wind is usually calmer.

signature.name: The Beehive
signature.detail: The distinctive round building of New Zealand's Parliament, a quick photo stop in the government district. Free guided tours of Parliament run on weekdays, so check times and book ahead.

signature.name: Yellow Crane Tower
signature.detail: Wuhan's most famous landmark, a reconstructed tower with sweeping views over the Yangtze River and the city. It is a symbol of the city and a must-see for first-time visitors. Tip: go early in the morning to avoid crowds and get clear views; the tower is easily reached by metro or taxi.

signature.name: East Lake
signature.detail: One of China's largest urban lakes, perfect for a relaxing walk, bike ride, or boat trip. The scenic area offers gardens, causeways, and plenty of spots for photography. Tip: visit on a weekday for fewer crowds; rent a bike to explore the lakeside paths.

signature.name: Hubei Provincial Museum
signature.detail: Home to an outstanding collection of ancient Chinese artifacts, including the famous bronze bells of Marquis Yi of Zeng. It's a great place to learn about the region's rich history. Tip: free entry but bring your passport; closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Wuhan University
signature.detail: A beautiful campus known for its cherry blossoms in spring and historic architecture. It's a pleasant place to stroll and soak up the academic atmosphere. Tip: cherry blossom season (late March) is extremely busy; visit early or outside peak times.

signature.name: Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge
signature.detail: The first bridge to span the Yangtze River, a major engineering feat and a symbol of modern Wuhan. Walking across offers great views of the river and city. Tip: walk or cycle across at sunset for the best views; the bridge is accessible from both sides.

signature.name: Guiyuan Temple
signature.detail: A serene Buddhist temple with intricate architecture and a peaceful atmosphere, offering a break from the bustling city. It's one of the most important temples in the region. Tip: dress respectfully and avoid loud clothing; open daily with a small entry fee.

signature.name: Han River, China
signature.detail: The Han River flows through Wuhan and offers scenic waterfront views, especially at night when the bridges are lit up. It's a nice place for an evening stroll. Tip: take a night cruise or walk along the riverside promenade for the best experience.

signature.name: Wuhan Greenland Center
signature.detail: A striking skyscraper that dominates the skyline, though it's primarily an office building. It's worth a look from the outside for architecture enthusiasts. Tip: not open for public observation, but you can admire it from nearby areas.

signature.name: Gulangyu Island
signature.detail: A car-free island of colonial villas, gardens and sea views, and Xiamen's most famous sight. Take the short ferry from the main island and go early in the morning to avoid the crowds; buy ferry tickets in advance.

signature.name: Nanputuo Temple
signature.detail: A large active Buddhist temple at the foot of the hills, with halls, gardens and a climb to viewpoints over the city and sea. Visit in the morning for cooler air and quieter halls; dress modestly and keep shoulders and knees covered.

signature.name: Terracotta Army
signature.detail: The buried army of thousands of life-size clay soldiers guarding China's first emperor is Xi'an's unmissable sight and one of the world's great archaeological discoveries. Go early in the morning to beat the tour groups, and book tickets online in advance since daily numbers are capped.

signature.name: Xi'an City Wall
signature.detail: The most complete ancient city wall in China forms a 14 km loop you can walk or cycle on top of, with great views over the old town. Rent a bike near the South Gate in late afternoon and stay for sunset; the wall is lit at night.

signature.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda
signature.detail: This Tang-dynasty Buddhist pagoda, built to house scriptures brought from India, anchors a lively square with a musical fountain show in the evening. Climb to the upper tiers for city views, and dress modestly if you enter the temple grounds.

signature.name: Muslim Quarter
signature.detail: A maze of lanes packed with street food, where the Hui Muslim community has traded for centuries. Come hungry in the evening for roujiamo and lamb skewers, and wander the side alleys away from the main tourist strip.

signature.name: Shaanxi History Museum
signature.detail: One of China's best museums, with treasures from the Tang dynasty and earlier that give context to everything else you see in Xi'an. Entry is free but limited, so reserve a timed ticket online days ahead; it is closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Bell Tower of Xi'an
signature.detail: The wooden tower at the exact center of the old city is a landmark you will pass constantly, and its upper gallery has fine views down the four main streets. Visit after dark when it is illuminated, and combine it with the Drum Tower opposite.

signature.name: Great Mosque of Xi'an
signature.detail: A working mosque hidden behind a wall in the Muslim Quarter, blending Islamic function with Chinese courtyard architecture. It is an active place of worship, so dress respectfully and avoid prayer times; the entrance is off Huajue Lane.

signature.name: Huaqing Palace
signature.detail: A hot-spring palace at the foot of Mount Li, famous for the Tang-dynasty love story of Emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei. It pairs naturally with the Terracotta Army on a day trip east of the city; go in the morning to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Daming Palace ruins
signature.detail: The vast site of the Tang dynasty's main imperial palace, now a landscaped park with excavated foundations and a good museum. It is spread out and sunny, so bring water and shade; it is a quiet contrast to the busy city center.

signature.name: Zagreb Cathedral
signature.detail: Croatia's tallest church and the city's defining spire, with a richly restored interior and a treasury. Go early morning to have the square in front mostly to yourself, and dress modestly since it is an active place of worship.

signature.name: St. Mark's Church
signature.detail: Famous for its brightly tiled roof bearing the city and national coats of arms, sitting on the cobbled heart of Gornji Grad. It is a short walk up from Ban Jelačić Square; check opening hours before going as interior access is limited.

signature.name: Gornji Grad
signature.detail: The old upper town of lanes, squares and historic buildings that gives Zagreb its character. Wander it on foot in the late afternoon, combining it with St. Mark's Church and the Stone Gate nearby.

signature.name: Ban Jelačić Square
signature.detail: The central square and meeting point of the city, ringed by cafés and the starting point for most walks. Come in the evening when it is liveliest, and use it as your orientation point for the lower town.

signature.name: Dolac Market
signature.detail: The colourful open-air market where locals buy produce, cheese and flowers. Arrive before noon for the fullest stalls, and bring small cash for the vendors.

signature.name: Stone Gate
signature.detail: A medieval gate that survived a fire and now shelters a shrine with a revered icon, still visited by pilgrims. It sits on the walk between the square and Gornji Grad, so it is easy to include on a walking route.

signature.name: Lotrščak Tower
signature.detail: A historic tower with a daily cannon firing at noon and views over the old town. Climb it around midday to catch the cannon, and note the small entry fee.

signature.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
signature.detail: A quirky, moving museum of objects donated after breakups, one of the city's most talked-about sights. It is compact, so allow about an hour; buy tickets on arrival.

signature.name: Mirogoj Cemetery
signature.detail: A grand park-like cemetery with arcades and domes, often described as an open-air gallery. It is a short bus or tram ride from the centre; go in daylight and dress for the weather.

signature.name: Song Mountain
signature.detail: A sacred Taoist mountain with dramatic peaks and historic temples, perfect for hiking and scenery. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water; the cable car saves time if you're short on energy.

signature.name: Henan Museum
signature.detail: One of China's best provincial museums, with treasures from ancient dynasties and a famous collection of bronze and jade. It's free with ID, closed on Mondays, and a good rainy-day option.

signature.name: Yellow River Scenic Area
signature.detail: See the mighty Yellow River up close, with viewpoints and a giant statue of the Yellow Emperor. It's a bit far from the city center, so allow half a day and check bus routes in advance.
