signature.name: Grossmünster
signature.detail: Zurich's iconic twin-towered Romanesque church, the legendary birthplace of the Reformation in German-speaking Switzerland. Climb the tower for sweeping views over the old town and lake. Go early morning to avoid crowds; modest dress recommended.

signature.name: Fraumünster Church
signature.detail: Famous for its stunning stained-glass windows by Marc Chagall and Augusto Giacometti, set in a serene Romanesque church. A must for art and architecture lovers. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter viewing; small entry fee for the church.

signature.name: Lindenhof
signature.detail: A tranquil hilltop square with Roman ruins and a lime tree, offering the best free panorama of the Limmat River and old town. Perfect for a picnic or sunset stroll. Reach it via short stairs from the river; go at dusk for romantic views.

food: About $118 a day for two cheap meals and one mid-range dinner
stay: Mid-range hotel about $374 a night for two
transport: About $39 a day: 4 transit rides and one 6 km taxi

signature.name: Ruins of St. Paul's
signature.detail: The facade of this 17th-century Jesuit church is the most photographed image in Macau and a symbol of the city's Portuguese heritage. It stands at the top of a steep granite stairway, with a museum of Christian art beneath it. Visit in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the largest crowds, and wear comfortable shoes for the climb.

signature.name: Senado Square
signature.detail: This paved square in the Historic Centre is lined with pastel colonial buildings and mosaic pavements. It is the easiest place to start a walk through the old town and to see the local mix of Portuguese and Chinese architecture. Go in the evening, when the buildings are lit and the square is lively, and reach it on foot from Ruins of St. Paul's.

signature.name: Guia Fortress
signature.detail: This 16th-century fort sits on Guia Hill and offers the best panoramic views over the old town and the peninsula. The chapel inside is one of the oldest surviving structures of its kind in the city. Take a bus or taxi up, or walk the hill path, and go before sunset for the views.

signature.name: A-Ma Temple
signature.detail: Dedicated to A-Ma, the sea goddess who is honoured as the protector of fishermen and sailors, this temple is said to give the city its name. Its granite courtyards and incense-filled halls are a good contrast to the colonial sights nearby. Go early on a weekday, dress modestly, and bring small change for the incense and offerings.

signature.name: Macau Tower
signature.detail: At 338 metres, this tower offers observation decks and a revolving restaurant with sweeping views over the city and the Pearl River Delta. The Sky Walk and bungy jumping are popular for thrill-seekers. Book observation tickets online ahead of time, especially for evening slots and weekends.

signature.name: Taipa Houses
signature.detail: These restored Portuguese-era houses on Taipa Island are now a small museum and cultural space that shows how the island's residents lived. They pair well with a stroll through nearby Taipa Village and its street market. Take a short taxi or bus ride from the Historic Centre and allow an hour or two.

food: Casual local meal $5-12; restaurant dinner $20-50
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $100-180 a night; casino resorts $150-300
transport: Bus $1-2 a ride; taxis $5-15 across town; ferries from Hong Kong $28 or more

signature.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo
signature.detail: This 19th-century casino is the glamorous heart of Monaco, set in the Monte-Carlo quarter with a grand facade and ornate interiors. Even if you do not gamble, the building and its gardens are worth a look. Dress smartly for the gaming rooms and check opening times and entry rules before you go; the main room is typically the one you pay to enter.

signature.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
signature.detail: The residence of the Grimaldi princes sits on the Rock of Monaco and gives the best views over the harbour. Visitors can see the State Apartments and the changing of the guard ceremony at noon. Arrive early in the day to avoid queues, and allow time for the walk up through the old town.

signature.name: Monaco Grand Prix Circuit
signature.detail: The street circuit that hosts the famous Formula One race winds through the city's streets, past the harbour and the casino. Outside race weekend you can walk or drive parts of the track and see the famous corners. Plan around the race calendar, since the streets are closed and crowded during the event.

signature.name: Oceanographic Museum
signature.detail: Founded by Prince Albert I, this museum combines marine science exhibits with an aquarium and a striking clifftop building. It is a good choice for families and rainy days. Buy tickets online ahead of peak season to skip the line.

signature.name: Saint Nicholas Cathedral
signature.detail: This Byzantine-style cathedral near the palace is the resting place of several Grimaldi princes, including Prince Rainier III and Princess Grace. Its striking mosaics and quiet interior offer a break from the busy streets. Modest dress is expected when visiting.

signature.name: Port Hercule
signature.detail: Monaco's main harbour is packed with superyachts and is a pleasant place to watch the boats and the Rock behind them. Walk the quay in the early evening for the best light. Boat cruises depart from around the harbour area.

food: Casual meal $20-35; upscale dining $100-250 a person
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $250-400 a night; luxury hotels much more
transport: Local bus about $2-3 a ride; taxis expensive; train or bus from Nice takes about 30-40 minutes

signature.name: Alhambra
signature.detail: The Nasrid palace complex on a hill above the city is Granada's defining sight, with intricate Islamic stucco, tiled courtyards and the Nasrid Palaces. Timed-entry tickets sell out, so book well ahead, especially for evening visits. Wear comfortable shoes, because the site is large and sloped.

signature.name: Generalife
signature.detail: The summer palace and gardens sit next to the Alhambra and are known for their water channels, terraces and cypress-lined paths. It is best seen in late afternoon, when the light is soft. Entry is usually bundled with Alhambra tickets, so check your booking.

signature.name: Albayzín
signature.detail: This hillside quarter of whitewashed lanes and cave-style houses has some of the best views of the Alhambra, especially from its miradors. Walk it in the late afternoon or at sunset. Wear sturdy shoes, as the streets are steep and cobbled.

signature.name: Sacromonte
signature.detail: Sacromonte is known for its hillside caves, historic Romani community and flamenco. Many cave venues host evening shows. Go by taxi or a guided tour after dark, since the lanes are steep and poorly lit.

signature.name: Granada Cathedral
signature.detail: The Renaissance cathedral in the city centre holds a richly decorated interior and a notable chapel. It is close to the Royal Chapel, so the two make an easy pairing. Visit in the morning, when the crowds are thinner.

signature.name: Royal Chapel of Granada
signature.detail: The Gothic-Renaissance chapel holds the tombs of Ferdinand and Isabella and the Catholic Monarchs. It is a short walk from the cathedral in the historic centre. Buy tickets at the entrance and allow about an hour.

signature.name: Corral del Carbón
signature.detail: This 14th-century former granary with a Moorish horseshoe arch is one of the few remaining Islamic-era buildings in the city centre. It is a quick stop on a walk through the old bazaar area. It is free to enter and easy to reach on foot.

food: Tapas with a drink $8-15; sit-down meal $15-30
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $100-160 a night; budget guesthouse $50-80
transport: City bus $1.50-2 a ride; taxis $5-12 across the centre; Alhambra shuttle bus about $2

signature.name: Budva Old Town
signature.detail: Budva's walled old town sits on the Adriatic and is the city's historic heart, with narrow stone streets, churches and sea walls to walk along. Go in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday crowds and heat in summer.

signature.name: Sveti Stefan
signature.detail: This former fishing village on a small islet joined to the mainland by a causeway is one of Montenegro's best-known views. It is mostly seen from outside, as access to the islet is restricted, so plan your visit around the viewpoints on the road.

signature.name: Sveti Stefan Beach
signature.detail: This beach lies in front of the Sveti Stefan islet and is popular for swimming and sunbathing with a view of the village. Arrive early in peak summer for a good spot, and bring water shoes for the pebbly shoreline.

signature.name: Kotor Old Town
signature.detail: Kotor's medieval walled town sits at the head of the Bay of Kotor and is a UNESCO-listed highlight within easy reach of Budva. Wear comfortable shoes, since the route up the city walls is steep, and visit mid-morning or after 4 pm when cruise groups are fewer.

signature.name: Perast
signature.detail: Perast is a small town of Venetian-era palaces on the Bay of Kotor, famous for its waterfront and the islets offshore. It is best reached by bus or tour, and an unhurried lunch on the promenade makes a good half-day stop.

signature.name: Bay of Kotor Cruise
signature.detail: A boat trip across the Bay of Kotor shows the mountains, towns and islands from the water, which is hard to see any other way. Book a morning departure for calmer water and clearer views, and check whether the cruise includes swimming stops.

signature.name: Skadar Lake National Park
signature.detail: This large lake on the Montenegro-Albania border is a protected wetland known for birdlife, water lilies and small islands. Boat tours leave from Virpazar and are the best way to explore, so book ahead in summer.

signature.name: Mausoleum of Njegoš on Lovćen
signature.detail: The mausoleum of the poet-prince Njegoš stands on Mount Lovćen above the Bay of Kotor, with wide views over the coast. The road up has many hairpin bends, so a guided tour or taxi is easier than driving yourself in poor weather.

food: Casual meal $10-18; seafood restaurants on the old town squares run $20-35
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $90-150 a night in summer; cheaper outside peak season
transport: Local buses about $1-2 a ride; taxis $3-6 for short trips; car hire is useful for the coast

signature.name: Rock of Gibraltar
signature.detail: The limestone promontory dominates the town and gives the territory its identity. Its upper slopes are a nature reserve, home to the famous Barbary macaques, and it offers wide views across the Strait toward Africa. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water, as the paths are steep and exposed.

signature.name: St. Michael's Cave
signature.detail: A large natural limestone cave system in the Upper Rock, known for its dramatic chambers and lighting. It is one of the most popular stops on the Rock. Go early in the day to avoid the midday crowds, and expect some steps and uneven ground.

signature.name: Gibraltar Great Siege Tunnels
signature.detail: A network of tunnels cut into the rock during the Great Siege of the 1780s, used for guns and observation. They give a vivid picture of the territory's military history. Book a guided visit where possible and allow around an hour.

signature.name: Moorish Castle
signature.detail: A fortification whose origins go back to Moorish rule, with later additions from other periods. It sits on the western slopes near the town and is well suited to a relaxed walk with views. Visit in the morning or late afternoon, when it is cooler.

signature.name: Gibraltar Cable Car
signature.detail: The cable car carries visitors from the town up to the Upper Rock, saving a steep climb and giving sweeping views. It is the simplest way to reach the top. Buy tickets online ahead of busy periods and check the schedule for wind closures.

signature.name: Main Street & Casemates Square
signature.detail: The pedestrian Main Street is the heart of the old town, lined with shops, cafes and British-style buildings. Casemates Square is a lively gathering point with restaurants. Visit in the evening when the square is busiest.

food: Casual meal $10-18; fish and chips about $12
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $150-230 a night
transport: Bus $1-2 a ride; cable car about $25-30 return; taxis short trips $5-10

signature.name: Promenade des Anglais
signature.detail: This long seafront promenade is the city's most famous walk, lined with palm trees, belle époque hotels and the pebble beach. It is best at sunset when the Baie des Anges glows. Walk it early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat, and bring water.

signature.name: Vieux Nice
signature.detail: The Old Town is a maze of ochre and pastel buildings, narrow lanes, churches and small squares full of cafés. Its lively atmosphere and local food make it the heart of Nice. Wander without a map, and go in the evening when the lanes are busiest.

signature.name: Castle Hill (Colline du Château)
signature.detail: This hilltop park offers the best panoramic views over the bay, the Old Town and the harbour. It also has waterfalls, shaded paths and ruins of an old castle. Reach it by the lift or stairs from the Old Town, and visit at sunset for the views.

signature.name: Cours Saleya Market
signature.detail: This open-air market sells flowers, fresh produce, olives and local specialities, and is set among restaurants in the Old Town. It is busiest in the morning and is a good place to see daily Niçois life. Go before noon, as stalls thin out by early afternoon.

signature.name: Place Masséna
signature.detail: This grand, sunny square, with its red and ochre facades and fountains, is the gateway between the Old Town and the modern city. It is a popular meeting point and a good spot for a coffee break. It is easy to reach on foot or by tram.

signature.name: Musée Matisse
signature.detail: This museum in the Cimiez hills holds a large collection of works by Henri Matisse, who lived and worked in Nice for decades. The villa and gardens are as appealing as the art. Check opening hours before going, as the museum is closed on some days, and reach it by bus.

signature.name: Musée Marc Chagall
signature.detail: This museum sits in the Cimiez hills and houses the largest public collection of Marc Chagall's Biblical Message paintings. The setting among pine trees makes it a calm visit. Pair it with the Matisse museum nearby, and check the schedule ahead of time.

signature.name: Èze Village
signature.detail: This medieval hilltop village above the sea is one of the Riviera's best-known sights, with stone lanes, galleries and views down to the coast. It is a short trip from Nice and is usually visited by bus or guided tour. Go early to avoid the day-tripper crowds, and wear comfortable shoes for the steep paths.

food: Casual meal $15-25; cafés and socca snacks $5-10
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $150-250 a night
transport: Tram about $2 a ride; taxis $15-30 across the centre

signature.name: Florence Cathedral
signature.detail: Santa Maria del Fiore is the city's defining landmark, crowned by Brunelleschi's red-tiled dome. Climbing the dome gives close views of the painted interior and the rooftops below. Dress with shoulders and knees covered, and book a dome-climb time slot in advance, since entry is timed and limited.

signature.name: Uffizi Gallery
signature.detail: One of the world's great art museums, it holds Botticelli's The Birth of Venus and Primavera along with major Renaissance paintings. The collection is large, so plan two to three hours. Book a timed entry ticket online, as same-day queues can be long.

signature.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
signature.detail: This is the home of Michelangelo's David, the marble statue that draws most visitors to Florence. Seeing it up close is a highlight of any trip. Reserve a timed-entry ticket ahead, because the museum often sells out.

signature.name: Ponte Vecchio
signature.detail: This medieval stone bridge over the Arno River is lined with jewelry shops and is one of the most photographed spots in Italy. It is best seen at sunrise or in the evening, when the crowds thin. It is an easy walk from the Uffizi and the Pitti Palace.

signature.name: Piazza della Signoria
signature.detail: This open square is the civic heart of Florence, with sculptures and the grand facade of the town hall around it. It is a good place to start a walking tour of the historic centre. Visit early in the morning for fewer people.

signature.name: Palazzo Vecchio
signature.detail: The city's medieval town hall dominates Piazza della Signoria with its tall tower and has served as the seat of Florentine government for centuries. Its interior rooms are rich with Renaissance decoration. Buy a ticket on site or online, and allow about an hour.

signature.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
signature.detail: This hilltop square on the south bank of the Arno offers the classic panoramic view over Florence and its cathedral dome. It is especially popular at sunset. You can walk up from the river or take a bus, then descend on foot.

food: Casual trattoria meal $15-25
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $150-250 a night
transport: City bus about $2 a ride; central sights are walkable

signature.name: Baščaršija
signature.detail: The old Ottoman bazaar quarter is the heart of Sarajevo, with copper workshops, tea houses and narrow cobbled lanes. It is the best place to understand the city's layered history. Visit in the morning or early evening for quieter streets and better light for photos.

signature.name: Latin Bridge
signature.detail: This small bridge is where Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in 1914, an event that helped trigger the First World War. A plaque and nearby exhibits mark the spot. It is a short walk from Baščaršija, so pair the two in one outing.

signature.name: Sebilj
signature.detail: This wooden Ottoman-style fountain stands in the main square of Baščaršija and has become one of the city's best-known images. It is a quick stop on any walk through the old town. Go early in the day to photograph it without crowds.

signature.name: Sarajevo City Hall (Vijećnica)
signature.detail: The Moorish Revival building was gutted by fire during the 1992-1995 siege and later restored, and it stands as a powerful symbol of the city's recovery. Its façade is one of the most striking in the centre. Check opening times in advance, as access to the interior can be limited.

signature.name: Gazi Husrev-bey Mosque
signature.detail: Built in the 16th century, this is the largest and most important mosque in Sarajevo and a centrepiece of Ottoman-era architecture. Visitors should dress modestly and remove shoes before entering. Visit outside prayer times and avoid Friday midday if you want a calmer visit.

signature.name: Sarajevo Tunnel Museum (Tunnel of Hope)
signature.detail: A section of the wartime tunnel that linked besieged Sarajevo to safe territory during the 1992-1995 siege is preserved here. The museum explains how it kept the city supplied and is a moving, essential visit for understanding recent history. Plan at least an hour, and consider a guided tour for context.

signature.name: Eternal Flame
signature.detail: This memorial flame honours fallen soldiers and is a focal point for ceremonies and remembrance in the city. It is a simple but meaningful stop, and it sits close to other central sights. Visit during the day for the clearest view, and treat it as a place of remembrance.

food: Casual meal $6-12; traditional ćevapi often $4-8
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $70-120 a night
transport: Tram about $0.50 a ride; taxis cheap; the old town is walkable

signature.name: Seville Cathedral
signature.detail: One of the largest Gothic cathedrals in the world, it holds the tomb of Christopher Columbus and a richly decorated interior. Its scale alone makes it a must-see for first-time visitors. Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid the heaviest crowds, and buy tickets online in advance.

signature.name: Alcázar of Seville
signature.detail: A working royal palace with Mudéjar palace halls, tiled courtyards and formal gardens that rank among Spain's finest. It is one of the most atmospheric places in the city. Book a timed entry ticket ahead, as queues can build up, and dress for walking outdoors.

signature.name: Giralda
signature.detail: The bell tower of the cathedral, originally built as a minaret, and the city's most recognisable landmark. Climbing it rewards you with wide views over the rooftops. Visit with the cathedral ticket, and wear comfortable shoes since the ascent is by ramp.

signature.name: Plaza de España, Seville
signature.detail: A grand half-circle of brick and tile built for the 1929 Ibero-American Exhibition, with canal-side bridges and painted alcoves for each province. It is especially photogenic in the golden hour. Reach it by walking through Parque de María Luisa, which is a short stroll away.

signature.name: Barrio de Santa Cruz
signature.detail: The old Jewish quarter, a maze of narrow lanes, orange-tree squares and whitewashed houses. It is the best area to wander and eat tapas. Visit in the cooler morning or evening, as the lanes get crowded at midday.

signature.name: Casa de Pilatos
signature.detail: A 16th-century palace blending Mudéjar and Renaissance styles, with azulejo-tiled patios and a lovely garden. It is a quieter alternative to the Alcázar. The ground floor entry ticket is inexpensive and can be bought online.

signature.name: Torre del Oro
signature.detail: A 13th-century riverside watchtower on the Guadalquivir, once used to guard the port and chain across the river. It is a short walk from the Triana Bridge and makes a good stop on a riverside walk. Go in the late afternoon for pleasant light on the water.

food: Tapas and casual meals $10-20 per person
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $110-180 a night
transport: Buses about $1.50 a ride; taxis affordable; the historic centre is very walkable

signature.name: Ba Na Hills Cable Car
signature.detail: Asia's longest cable car climbs to the Ba Na Hills, a mountain resort with French-inspired architecture and themed gardens. The ride itself offers wide views over the forest and coast. Book tickets in advance and go early in the day to avoid queues at the top.

signature.name: Golden Bridge
signature.detail: A pedestrian bridge held up by giant stone hands, perched on the Ba Na Hills, and one of the most photographed sights in Vietnam. It is best seen early morning, before the crowds and haze build up. Wear comfortable shoes, as the walk includes steps and uneven stone.

signature.name: Sun World Ba Na Hills
signature.detail: The amusement park at the top of the hills, known as Fantasy Park, offers many rides, attractions and themed areas. It is the main reason many visitors stay for a full day. Combine it with the cable car ticket to save time and money.

signature.name: Marble Mountains
signature.detail: A cluster of marble hills with caves, tunnels and Buddhist shrines, with climbs offering views over the coast. It is a short trip from the city centre. Wear sturdy shoes and cover your shoulders when entering temples.

signature.name: Lady Buddha
signature.detail: A huge white statue of the Goddess of Mercy on the Son Tra Peninsula, overlooking the sea and the city. It is one of the most recognisable landmarks in Da Nang. Visit in the morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer visitors, and dress modestly.

signature.name: My Khe Beach
signature.detail: A long sandy beach with calm water, often cited as one of the best in Vietnam. It is ideal for a relaxed swim or sunset walk. Go in the early morning or late afternoon, as the midday sun is strong.

signature.name: Dragon Bridge, Da Nang
signature.detail: A steel bridge shaped like a dragon that spans the Han River, famous for fire and water displays on weekend nights. It is a lively spot in the evening. Arrive before dark to find a viewing spot along the riverbank.

signature.name: Hai Van Pass
signature.detail: A winding mountain road with dramatic views over the coastline, linking Da Nang with Hue. It is best experienced by motorbike, car or the scenic train. Go on a clear day for the best views, as cloud often covers the summit.

food: Local bowl of mi quang or pho $2-4; mid-range seafood dinner $10-20
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $60-120 a night
transport: Grab rides $2-6 across the city; motorbike rental $6-10 a day
